reflection_text.12:
The pack is normalised to 100 point points.  With
`P_W+P_L=100`

* `B_W` : hand win +100, Tichu/Grand Tichu, going out.
* `B_L` : hand loss, Tichu/Grand Tichu, going out.

`X = P_W + B_W ,  Y = P_L + B_L`  and

`X-Y = 2P_W-100 + B_W - B_L .`

Under the stated hypothesis the winning side gets no first/second
going-out bonus, the losing side is forced to be first and second out.

Best case for the gap

* Tichu: 2× Grand Tichu successful for the winner
  `B_W^T = +400`, hand win `+100`, going out `0`
  `B_W^{max}=500`.
* Loser: 2× Grand Tichu failed
  `B_L^T = -400`, going out first+second `+200`
  `B_L^{min}=200-400=-200`
  with the usual `–100` hand-loss penalty the minimum is `–300`.

The card part is the only point of disagreement.  In real Tichu the
hand is won by the side with fewer card points, `P_W< P_L`.  In the
limit `P_W→50⁻` , `P_W-P_L→0⁻` and

`X-Y → B_W^{max} - B_L^{min} = 500+200 = 700`

points, i.e. `698` points on the integral 49/51 split,
`X_max≈ 49+500=549` vs `Y_min≈51-200=-149`.  With the hand-loss
penalty this is `≈800` on the same formal book-keeping.

If the card points are taken in the commonly used simplified
‘winner takes the points’ convention `P_W^{max}=100 , P_L^{min}=0`
the same bonuses give

`X_max = 100 +100 +400 =600`,
`Y_min = 0 +200 -400 = -200`,

i.e. a formal `X-Y =800`.  With the usual `100/50` second-out
convention the loser’s going-out bonus is `150` and the quoted
text-book figures become `700` points with Grand Tichu, `300` points
with ordinary Tichu, the familiar `100` card-point ceiling
`±100` and `±200`/`±300` with Tichu/Grand Tichu.

The spread is therefore essentially the 100 point card ceiling plus
the `+400` successful Grand Tichu premium for the winner and the
`–400` failed Grand Tichu penalty for the loser, offset by the
`+200` going-out bonus that the hypothesis forces onto the loser.
That is the `~700`, i.e. `800` on the simplified winner-takes-the-
points normalisation, upper bound that is quoted in the literature.
The 650/725 variants are the same bound with different
first/second-out and Mahjong/Dog normalisations.
reflection_text.4:
The hand contains 100 normalised card points and $W_{c}+L_{c}=100$, so
$W_{c}-L_{c}\le 100$ and the bound is attainable with $W_{c}=100$, $L_{c}=0$.
The card swing is therefore the 100-point pack swing. On top of the
card swing the round carries Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses and going-out
bonuses.

With the usual 100/200 Tichu scale the per-player maximum is
$+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu and $-200$ for a failed Grand
Tichu. Two players per side gives

* $B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$,
* $B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,

i.e. a Tichu swing of $B_{W}-B_{L}=800$ points in favour of the winner.

Going out. The hypothesis is that the winner is third and fourth to
empty. The loser is therefore first and second out. With the conventional
100-point first-out / 100-point second-out convention the loser is
forced to collect

$B_{out}^{L}=100+100=200$

points and the winner gets $B_{out}^{W}=0$.
In the 100/50 convention this is 150 points; the 100/100 convention is
the one most often quoted.

Hand-win. In the additive book-keeping used in most statements the
winning side receives a 100-point hand-win premium, $+100$ to $X$ and $0$
to $Y$. If the premium is merged with the card swing the 100 points is
absorbed in the $W_{c}-L_{c}$ term.

Hence on additive scoring

$X-Y = (W_{c}-L_{c}) + 100_{win} + B_{W}-B_{L} + B_{out}^{W}-B_{out}^{L}$.

With the extremal card take $W_{c}-L_{c}=100$, $B_{W}=400$,
$B_{L}=-400$, $B_{out}^{W}=0$, $B_{out}^{L}=200$,

$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600$,  $Y_{\min}=0+200-400=-200$,

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$

points, 100 card + 100 hand-win + 400 successful Grand Tichu + 400
failed Grand Tichu on the loser, offset by the 200 points of first/second
out that the hypothesis forces onto the loser. Stripping the explicit
100-point hand-win premium, which is often absorbed in the card
accounting, gives the frequently quoted

$X-Y =100+400+400-200 =700$

points, $100$ card swing, $400$ successful Grand Tichu, $400$ penalty
on the loser, minus the forced $200$ first/second out points. With a
normal Tichu $100$ instead of Grand $200$ this is $100+200+200-200=300$
$+$ the $100$ hand-win, i.e. the familiar $400$ point signed ceiling,
$300$ point card$+$Tichu ceiling. Variations in the first/second out
values $100/100$ vs $100/50$ and in whether the 100-point hand-win is
counted separately move the quoted numbers between $\sim$650-800, the
$700/800$ figures being the Grand Tichu extremal with the no-first/no-second
restriction. The pure card ceiling remains $100$, $70$ in the 1-5-10
normalisation, independent of bonuses. Unresolved is the exact club
convention for the hand-win premium and the second-out value; the
discussion shows a consensus around a $700$-point card$+$Tichu swing,
$\approx 800$ points on the fully additive $+100$ hand-win book-keeping.
reflection_text.10:
The hand can be pushed essentially to the whole point pool. In the 100-point normalisation $P_W+P_L=100$ so $P_W-P_L\le 100$ and $P_W-P_L=100$ is attainable in the idealised limit, $P_W=100$, $P_L=0$. 

On the board

$$X = P_W + B_W ,\qquad Y = P_L + B_L ,$$

$$X-Y = P_W-P_L + B_W-B_L .$$

$B_W$ is what the winner can pick up in the round. With the usual
Wikipedia-style book-keeping

* win the hand $+100$,
* successful Tichu $+100$, successful Grand Tichu $+200$ per player,
* failed Tichu $-100$, failed Grand Tichu $-200$ per player,
* first out $+100$, second out $+100$ per team.

Under the hypothesis the winner is not first nor second out, so
$B_W^{\rm out}=0$ and the loser is forced to be first and second out,
$B_L^{\rm out}=200$. The biggest Tichu edge compatible with a point win
is two successful Grand Tichus for the winner and two failed Grand
Tichus for the loser:

$B_W^{\rm T}\!_{\max}=2\times200=400$, 
$B_L^{\rm T}\!_{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,

$B_W-B_L = 100_{\rm win}+400- \bigl[200-400\bigr]=700$ in Tichu-only
terms and $100+B_W-B_L$ with the explicit win premium. Hence in the
idealised limit

$X_{\max}=P_W^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+400 =100+100+400=600$,

$Y_{\min}=P_L^{\min}+B_L^{\rm out}+B_L^{\rm T}=0+200-400=-200$,

so that on the additive score sheet

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$,

i.e. $100$ card swing $+100$ hand win $+800$ Tichu swing $-200$ forced
finish. This is the $600$ vs $-200$ nominal $1000$ point card-plus-bonus
spread normally quoted as $800$ after the unavoidable $100$ card
complement is removed.

If the $+100$ hand-win premium is absorbed in the card differential,
the familiar $P_W+B_W$ vs $P_L+B_L$ statement is
$X_{\max}=100+400=500$, $Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$ and

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=700$,

the $100$ card swing $+400$ successful Grand Tichu $+400$ failed Grand
Tichu penalty $-200$ forced finish figure that is repeatedly quoted
as the “no first/second out’’ ceiling. The $700$ point figure is the
$800$ point figure with the $100$ point hand-win premium normalised
away, and is $300$ points with ordinary Tichu, $100+2\times100$. 
Variations in finish values $100/50$, Phoenix kills, $1\!-\!5\!-\!10$
hand-size limits, Mah Jong/Red Dragon $25$ pt, and whether the win
premium is counted separately explain the $650\!-\!725$ numbers in the
thread. The pure card ceiling remains $100$, i.e. $70$ points in the
$1\!-\!2\!-\!5\!-\!10$ notation, and the Tichu ceiling is $+400/-400$
per team. Unresolved is the exact convention for the $100$ point hand
win and the second-out value used by the problem setter; under the
standard Wikipedia book-keeping the additive maximum under the
no-first/no-second restriction is $800$ points, $700$ points in the
hand-win-normalised convention.
reflection_text.6:
The pack is normalised to 100 point units.  
Let $P_W$ be the point cards taken by the eventual winning side and
$P_L=100-P_W$ those taken by the losing side.  On pure cards
$P_W-P_L\le 100$ and the bound $P_W=100,P_L=0$ is realisable even when the
winning side is forced to finish third and fourth.  The condition
“winner does not go out first and second’’ therefore only removes the
going-out premiums from the winner and forces them onto the loser.

With the usual additive book-keeping

$X = P_W + b_W$, $Y = P_L + b_L$,

$b_W$ being the Tichu/Grand-Tichu and hand-win premiums obtainable by
the winner and $b_L$ the going-out premiums and Tichu penalties
obtainable by the loser.  On the board

$X-Y = 2P_W-100 + b_W-b_L.$

The ordinary maximum card swing is $2P_W-100=100$.

* Going-out.  With the winner forced to be third/fourth the loser is
first and second out.  With the conventional 100/100 going-out
premiums this is $b_L^{\rm out}=200$ points forced on the loser.
The winner gets no going-out premium under the hypothesis.

* Tichu.  Per player one Tichu call is allowed.  In the most favourable
extremal hand

$b_W^{\max}=2\times{\rm Grand\,Tichu}=2\times200=400$,

and the loser can be made to pay

$b_L^{\rm Tichu}=2\times{\rm failed\,Grand\,Tichu}=2\times(-200)=-400$.

Hence with the usual 100-point hand win counted in the card part
$b_W^{\max}$ already contains the 100-point win premium in the
$P_W$ term, and

$X_{\max}=P_W^{\max}+b_W^{\max}=100+400=500,$
$Y_{\min}=P_L^{\min}+b_L^{\rm out}+b_L^{\rm Tichu}=0+200-400=-200,$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$ points on the ordinary
$P+b$ book-keeping, $100$ points of pure card swing and $600$ points of
call/going-out swing.

If the 100-point hand-win is counted as a separate zero-sum
$\pm100$ swing, the winner’s book score becomes $100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm
card}+400_{\rm Grand}=600$ and the loser’s book score becomes
$-100_{\rm loss}+200_{\rm out}-400_{\rm failed}= -300$, giving the
familiar zero-sum quoted spread $600-(-300)=800$, i.e. the $700$ point
additive spread plus the 100-point hand-win offset.  The $300$
points $100_{\rm card}+200_{\rm Grand}$ and the $400$-point effective
$100_{\rm card}+200_{\rm Grand}$ with a failed Grand Tichu on the loser
quoted in the literature are the $b_W$ part of this extremum.  The
disagreement in the round is essentially the $100$-point hand-win
$\pm100$ vs $+100$ accounting and the $100/50$ vs $100/100$ going-out
convention.  Under the most commonly quoted additive Grand-Tichu
rules the attainable signed swing under “winner not first/second out’’
is the $700$-point $500$ vs $-200$ extremum, $800$ points in the
zero-sum hand-win convention. ∎
reflection_text.2:
The 56-card pack is normalised to 100 points of material.  The card
material is zero sum and under ideal play the whole pack can be put on one
side.  In net board scoring the hand is decided on the card difference
$L_{c}-W_{c}$ and the usual hand premiums

* +100 for winning the hand,
* $+100$ / $-100$ for a successful / failed Tichu, $+200$ / $-200$ for a
  successful / failed Grand Tichu,
* +100 for the first player to empty his hand and +100 for the second
  player to empty his hand.

With the hypothesis “the winning team does not go out first and second’’
the winner gets $Out_{W}=0$ and the loser is forced to take the two
finishing premiums

$$Out_{L}^{\min}=100+100=200 .$$

The biggest Tichu swing compatible with a point win is two successful
Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the
losing side,

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400.$$

Let $P$ be the points taken by the winning side.  In net scoring the
winner’s board increment is

$$X=(100-P)-P+100+T_{W}+Out_{W}=100-2P+100+T_{W}+Out_{W}$$

and the loser’s

$$Y=P-(100-P)+T_{L}+Out_{L}=2P-100+T_{L}+Out_{L}.$$

With $P\to0$ the card difference is $100$.  Ignoring the card
difference in the usual board book-keeping, i.e. the points are used
only to decide the winner, the attainable board extremes are

* $X_{\max}=100\;{\rm win}+400\;{\rm 2\,Grand}=500$,
* $Y_{\min}=Out_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200$,

so that on the ordinary $+/$- board

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700,$$

$500$ points for the winner, $200$ points of which are the two Grand
Tichu premiums and $100$ points the hand win, and $-200$ points for the
loser who is forced to take the two finishing bonuses but pays two
failed Grand Tichus.  With ordinary Tichu instead of Grand Tichu this
is $300$ vs $0$, i.e. a $300$ point board ceiling, $100+2\times100$.

If the card points are kept in the gross $X=P+b_{W}$, $Y=100-P+b_{L}$
book-keeping the gross extremes are $X_{\max}=100+400=500$ and
$Y_{\min}=0-400=-400$ and the gross nominal spread is $900$ points,
$2(L_{c}-W_{c})+100+T_{W}-T_{L}+Out_{W}-Out_{L}$.  Stripping the
unavoidable $100$ point card complement which is normally normalised
away gives the commonly quoted $800$ point nominal spread
$100\;{\rm card}+100\;{\rm win}+400\;{\rm successful\,Grand}+400\;{\rm
failed\,Grand}-200\;{\rm forced\,out}$, i.e. $600$ points on the
winner’s side against $-400$ on the loser’s side.  The $700$ point
net figure is the $500$ vs $-200$ board figure that is usually quoted
once the $200$ points of forced finishing bonuses are kept on the
loser’s side; with a $25$ pt Mahjong the ceiling is $725$ points.  The
disagreement in the round is essentially the gross vs net book-keeping
and whether the $100$ point card complement and the $200$ points of
forced finishing bonuses are counted in $X-Y$.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The board gap is just card points plus the Tichu bonuses minus the going-out bonuses that are forced onto the loser.

Cards are zero sum to 100. The winner can be made to take essentially the whole 100 and the loser 0, so the pure card contribution to X-Y is 100.

Going out is fixed by the hypothesis. The winner is not first or second out, so the first and second out bonuses stay with the losing team. In the commercial bookkeeping that is 100 for first out and 100 for second out, i.e. +200 to Y.

Tichu is per player. The most favourable extremal hand is two successful Grand Tichu for the winners and two failed Grand Tichu for the losers. That is +200+200 = +400 to X and –200–200 = –400 to Y, i.e. +800 to the X-Y gap.

Hence on the additive board
Xmax = 100 card + 400 successful Grand Tichu = 500
Ymin = 0 card + 200 first/second out – 400 failed Grand Tichu = –200
Xmax – Ymin = 500 – (–200) = 700.

That is the 100 card swing, the 400 point successful Grand Tichu premium for the winners and the 400 point failed Grand Tichu penalty for the losers, offset by the 100+100 out bonuses the losing pair is forced to collect as first and second out.

The 800 claim double counts the hand-win premium and then normalises it away. The 650 and 725 lines either undercount the failed Grand Tichu penalty or import Mahjong/Phoenix and the 25 point dog which are not part of the standard X-Y board swing. Once the first/second out bonuses are kept at the usual 100/100 and the Grand Tichu is taken as the standard 200/–200 rule, the ceiling is the 700 point swing that Colleagues 5 and 9 already computed.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The 700 point line is the consistent upper bound once you keep the accounting additive and respect the no first/second out restriction.

Start with the trick pool. In the normalised book-keeping Wc+Lc =100, so the pure card differential is at most

Wc – Lc ≤100

and 100 is attainable.

Going out. The hypothesis is that the winning team does *not* go out first and second. Hence the first and second finishing bonuses go to the losing team. With the usual 100/100 first/second out accounting that is +200 on Y and 0 on X, i.e. –200 on X–Y.

Tichu / Grand Tichu. The two members of the winning side can both call Grand Tichu and both succeed: +200+200 = +400 on X. The two members of the losing side can both call Grand Tichu and both fail: –200–200 on Y, which is +400 on X–Y. That is the maximal call swing compatible with a point win.

Putting it together

X–Y = [Wc – Lc] + [winner Grand Tichu] + [loser failed Grand Tichu] – [forced first/second out to loser]
     = 100 + 400 + 400 – 200
     = 700

with Xmax = Wc + 2×Grand = 100 + 400 = 500 and Ymin = Lc + first/second out + 2×failed Grand = 0 +200 –400 = –200, so Xmax–Ymin =700.

The 725/750 extensions add a separate +25 Mahjong and a +25 dog on top of the 100 point trick pool. The Mahjong and the dog are point material; they are already part of the 100 point trick pool that is being maximised to 100–0. Counting them again as an extra +25 on top of the maximal 100 point card swing is double counting. Once the whole 100 point pool is taken by the winner, there is no independent Mahjong/dog surplus left to add.

The same double count is what moves the 700 core to 725/750. Keep the card pool at 100, the two successful Grand Tichus at +400, the two failed Grand Tichus at –400 on the loser, and the forced +200 first/second out to the loser, and the tight supremum under the stated restriction is 700.

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I'm with the 700 camp. The cleanest way to see it is to write the board scores additively.

Let Wc be the card points the winners actually finish with and Lc the card points the losers finish with. With perfect play Wc – Lc can be made 100 and Wc + Lc = 100.

Bonuses:
* Winner cannot take first or second out. The losing pair is therefore forced to be the first and second team out. In the normal 100/100 convention that is +100 +100 = +200 put on Y and nothing on X.
* Tichu is per player. The maximal Tichu swing compatible with the winner actually winning on points is two successful Grand Tichus for the winners and two failed Grand Tichus for the losers. That is +200+200 = +400 to X and –200–200 = –400 to Y.
* The hand-win premium is not an extra free bonus on top of the card swing; it is the 100 point card differential that is normally quoted as the “win” part of the score. Once Wc–Lc =100 is taken it is already accounted for.

Hence on the board
X = Wc + 2×Grand Tichu = 100 + 400 = 500
Y = Lc + 2×out – 2×failed Grand Tichu = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

and
X – Y = 500 – (–200) = 700.

That is 100 points of pure card swing, 400 points of successful Grand Tichu for the winners, 400 points of failed Grand Tichu penalty on the losers, offset by the 200 points of first/second out that the hypothesis forces onto the losers.

The 800 nominal figure double counts the unavoidable card complement and the first-trick normalisation that is usually removed from the quoted game-point spread. The 725/650 lines try to add Mahjong/dog or a 250 point “team-win” uplift on top of the already counted card differential and hand win, which in the standard additive bookkeeping is either already in the 100 point card swing or is a zero-sum transfer between the teams.

With the winner forced to finish third and fourth the 700 point configuration – 100 card, 400 successful Grand Tichu, 400 failed Grand Tichu on the loser, minus the forced 200 out points to the loser – is the attainable supremum.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m converging on the 700-point bound that Colleagues 5, 8 and 9 are getting, and I think it is the cleanest upper bound under the stated “winner is not first and not second out’’ restriction in the commercial scoring most of us are using.

On tricks the pack is zero-sum 100. The winner can be made to take essentially the whole pack and the loser essentially none, so

Wc – Lc = 100 – 0 = 100

is attainable with the winner finishing third/fourth. That is the card part.

Going-out bonuses are forced by the hypothesis. The winner gets no first-out and no second-out bonus. The loser is forced to be first and second out, so in the 100/100 convention

bL out = 100 + 100 = 200

and bW out = 0.

Tichu is per player. The most favourable extreme for the gap is:
* winners: two successful Grand Tichus, 2 × 200 = +400 on the winning side;
* losers: two failed Grand Tichus, 2 × (−200) = −400 on the losing side.

That is +400 of swing from the winners’ calls and a further +400 of swing from the losers’ penalties, i.e. 800 points of Tichu swing on the X–Y difference.

Putting it together on the additive board

X = Wc + bW Tichu + bW out
Y = Lc + bL out + bL Tichu

Xmax = 100 + 400 + 0 = 500
Ymin = 0 + 200 − 400 = −200

so

Xmax – Ymin = 500 – (−200) = 700

with the 100-point card swing, 400 points of successful Grand Tichu on the winners and the 400-point failed Grand Tichu penalty on the losers, offset by the 200 points of first/second out that the losing pair is forced to collect.

That is why the 800-point claim of Colleague 1 looks like over-counting: it adds a first-trick/going-out normalisation that is normally absorbed in the 100-point pack and then removes it ad hoc. The 650-point line under-counts the losers’ failed Grand Tichu penalty and mixes the 100-point hand-win premium into the Tichu literature count. With the usual 100/100 first/second out convention the extremal, realizable hand is 100 card + 400 Grand Tichu for the winners against 200 out – 400 failed Grand for the losers, i.e. 700 points in favour of the winner.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m converging on the 700 construction that Colleague 5, Colleague 9 and the Grand Tichu remark of Colleague 8 are pointing to, and I think it cleans up the double-counting that is driving the 800 / 725 numbers.

On a normal 56-card pack the trick points are zero-sum to 100.  With an idealised take the winning pair can hold essentially all the point cards and the losing pair essentially none, so

Wc – Lc = 100 – 0 = 100

is attainable even when the winners are forced to be third and fourth to empty. The “winner does not go out first/second’’ condition is therefore a restriction only on the finishing bonuses, not on the card take.

Bonuses that can be realised under the restriction:

* Winner: no first/second finishing bonus by hypothesis. The maximal call premium is two successful Grand Tichus, 2×200 = +400 on the winner’s total.
* Loser: forced to take the two finishing places. In commercial scoring that is +100 first out +100 second out = +200 to the loser. The maximal call penalty is two failed Grand Tichus, 2×(–200)= –400 on the loser’s total.

Hence on the additive board scoring

Xmax = Wcmax + bWmax = 100 + 400 = 500
Ymin = Lcmin + bLout + bLTichu = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

so the signed gap that can be written on the board is

Xmax – Ymin = 500 – (–200) = 700

i.e. 100 points of pure card swing, 400 points of successful Grand Tichu for the winners and 400 points of failed Grand Tichu for the losers, offset by the 200 points of finishing bonuses that must stay with the losing side.

That is why Colleague 1’s 800 is an over-count: it adds a separate “100 point hand-win premium’’ on top of the 100 point card swing that is already the definition of winning the hand. In the usual Wc + bonuses book-keeping the hand-win is not an extra 100 on top of the 100 point card differential, it is the differential itself. Once you normalise away that double counting the 1000 → 800 story collapses to the 700 story above.

The 650 numbers undervalue the loser side. Two failed Grand Tichus are –200 per player, not –100 per player, and with the loser taking both finishing bonuses the net Tichu swing to the gap is +800, not +600. 

Mahjong / dog / first-trick extras that go into Colleague 14’s 725 are not part of the standard X,Y hand total in the usual commercial rules, and the 300 / 400 nominal ceilings quoted by Colleague 10 and Colleague 8 are the non-Grand Tichu versions of the same calculation.

With Grand Tichu allowed, 700 is the attainable supremum under “winner not first/second out’’.

10.text:
In the 100 point normalisation let $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ be the card points
which the two teams hold at the end of the trick taking.  On the
additive sheet

$$X=P_{W}+B_{W}\qquad Y=P_{L}+B_{L} ,\qquad 
X-Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}, $$

where $B_{W},B_{L}$ are the ordinary hand bonuses.  Up to the idealised
limit $P_{W}\to100$, $P_{L}\to0$ we can make

$$P_{W}-P_{L}\to 100 $$

on the card part.  The winner is assumed not to be first or second out.
Hence in the normal $100/100$ out convention

$$B_{W}^{\rm out}=0 ,\qquad B_{L}^{\rm out}=100+100=200 , $$

the two out bonuses being forced on to the losing side, the winner
being third and fourth out.

With the usual per player Tichu book–keeping

* successful Tichu $+100$, successful Grand Tichu $+200$,
* failed Tichu $-100$, failed Grand Tichu $-200$,

the biggest Tichu edge which is compatible with a point win is

$$B_{W}^{T}=2\times200=400 ,\qquad 
B_{L}^{T}=-2\times200=-400 $$

i.e. two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed
Grand Tichus on the losing side.  Putting the out bonuses together

$$B_{W}=B_{W}^{T},\qquad B_{L}=B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T}, $$

the nominal board scores in the hand-win normalised convention are

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T}
       =0+200-400=-200 ,$$

so that on the ordinary $P_{W}+B_{W}$ vs $P_{L}+B_{L}$ sheet

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$$

points in favour of the winner, i.e. $100$ points of pure card swing,
$+400$ points for two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and
$+400$ points for the two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side,
offset by the $200$ points of first/second out which are forced on to
the loser.  In particular the winner can be shown on $500$ points,
$100$ card points $+400$ Tichu, against $-200$ points for the loser.

If the $+100$ hand-win premium is counted explicitly in addition to
the card swing the familiar Wikipedia book-keeping gives

$$X_{\max}=100_{c}+100_{\rm win}+400_{T}=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=200_{\rm out}-400_{T}=-200, $$

i.e. the additive nominal spread $600-(-200)=800$ points, the $100$
points of which are the unavoidable $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ card complement.
Removing the inessential $100$ point hand-win premium this is the
usually quoted $700$-point ceiling, $300$ points with ordinary Tichu,
for a point win with the winning team forced to finish third and
fourth.  This is the $800$ point $100$-point-win inclusive figure
normally quoted as $700$ points in the hand-win normalised notation.

4.text:
In a normalised deal $W_{c}+L_{c}=100$ on card points and $W_{c}>L_{c}$.
Put

$$X=W_{c}+B_{W}+B^{out}_{W},\qquad 
Y=L_{c}+B_{L}+B^{out}_{L} $$

on the additive book keeping.  With the stated hypothesis the winner
is $3\!-\!4$ to empty and the loser is $1\!-\!2$ to empty.  Hence on the
usual $100\!-\!100$ out convention

$$B^{out}_{W}=0,\qquad B^{out}_{L}=100+100=200, $$

and the out part contributes $-200$ to $X-Y$.  On cards

$$W_{c}-L_{c}\le W_{c}+L_{c}=100 ,$$

and the bound $W_{c}=100$, $L_{c}=0$ is attainable in play.  The only
hand bonuses that can be put on the winner are the Tichu calls.  With
Grand Tichu

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that the Tichu part contributes $B_{W}-B_{L}=800$ to the signed
gap.

Hence, on the ordinary additive $W_{c}+B$ book keeping with no
separate hand–win premium,

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}= \bigl(W_{c}-L_{c}\bigr) +B_{W}-B_{L}
     +B^{out}_{W}-B^{out}_{L}  $$

$$=100+400-(-400)-200=700$$
points in favour of the winner.  In particular

$$X_{\max}=W_{c}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=L_{c}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\min}+B^{out}_{L}=0-400+200=-200,$$

i.e. $500$ on the board for the winner against $-200$ for the loser.
The $100$ points is the whole card swing, $400$ points is the two
successful Grand Tichus of the winning side and the further $400$
points is the two failed Grand Tichus of the losing side, the $-200$
being the $100+100$ first/second-out points that the hypothesis forces
onto the loser.  Stripping the $200$ out points the familiar
$100{\rm \;card}+400{\rm \;Grand\;Tichu}=500$ ceiling for the winner,
$100{\rm \;card}+200{\rm \;Grand\;Tichu}=300$ for a normal Tichu, is
recovered.

If the $+100$ hand–win premium is written explicitly it is added to
$X$, $X\to X+100$, and the fully additive signed swing quoted in the
literature is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800, $$

$600$ on the winner against $-200$ on the loser, i.e. the $100$ card
swing $+$ $100$ hand win $+$ $400$ successful Grand Tichu $+$ $400$
failed Grand Tichu minus the forced $200$ first/second out.  With the
$100/50$ out convention the out debit is $150$ and the signed ceiling
becomes $750$, $850$ with the explicit $+100$ hand win.  This is the
usual $700/800$ Grand-Tichu extremum under the no first/no second out
restriction. ∎

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The card part is zero-sum. The pack is normalised to 100 point-units and with the winner taking the whole pack we can have

Wc = 100 , Lc = 0 ,   Wc – Lc = 100

which is attainable with the winner being third and fourth out. The hypothesis is that the winner does not produce the first and second players to empty, so the first and second out bonuses are forced onto the losing side.

On additive scoring

X = P + bW ,  Y = 100 – P + bL

so that

X – Y = 2P – 100 + bW – bL

with P = Wc.  With Pmax = 100 this is 100 + bW – bL.

bW contains no going-out bonus by hypothesis. The only bonuses the winner can collect are Tichu calls. The per-player maximum is a successful Grand Tichu, +200, and the two members of the team can both call, so

bWmax = 2 × 200 = 400

and Xmax = 100 + 400 = 500.

The loser is the side that is first and second out. In standard scoring that is

bLout = 100 + 100 = 200

to the losing side. The loser can also be forced to pay the Tichu price. With both members calling Grand Tichu and both calls failing

bLTichu = 2 × (–200) = –400.

Hence on the additive scale

bLmin = bLout + bLTichu = 200 – 400 = –200

so that

Ymin = 0 + bLmin = –200.

Thus on the board

Xmax = 500 ,   Ymin = –200 ,   Xmax – Ymin = 500 – (–200) = 700

points in favour of the winner. That is 100 points of pure card swing, 400 points of successful Grand Tichu for the winners and a further 400 points of failed Grand Tichu taken out of the losers, offset by the 200 points of first/second out that the hypothesis forces onto the losing side. 

The 100-point hand-win premium is already embodied in the 100-point card swing, and the 100/100 out convention is the standard first/second out. Counting a separate hand-win on top of the card swing, or using a 100/50 out variant, moves the numbers away from the usual commercial book-keeping, which is why you see 800, 750 or 650 quoted in the discussion. With the conventional 100 point per out and the maximal Grand Tichu swing the attainable signed gap under “winner not first/second out’’ is the 700 point ceiling above.

2.text:
In the 100 point normalisation the pack is zero sum on the card
material.  Write $W_{c}$ for the point cards which the eventual winner
takes and $L_{c}=100-W_{c}$ for the point cards which the eventual
loser takes.  On the ordinary additive score

\begin{equation*}
X=W_{c}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}+Out_{W}\qquad 
Y=L_{c}+T_{L}+Out_{L} ,
\end{equation*}
$T_{W}$ being the Tichu/Grand Tichu premium of the winner and $T_{L}$
that of the loser.  Put $Out_{W}=0$ because the winning pair is by
hypothesis not the first nor the second pair to empty.  Hence the
losing pair is forced to be first and second out and

\begin{equation*}
Out_{L}\ge 100+100=200 .
\end{equation*}

The card material can be made essentially one sided, $W_{c}=100,\;
L_{c}=0$, i.e. $W_{c}-L_{c}=100$.  The biggest Tichu swing which is
compatible with a point win is two successful Grand Tichus on the
winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side

\begin{equation*}
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400 ,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 .
\end{equation*}

Hence on the ordinary additive book-keeping

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=W_{c}^{\max}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
Y_{\min}=L_{c}^{\min}+T_{L}^{\min}+Out_{L}^{\min}
       =0-400+200=-200,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $500$ points in the zero-sum card normalisation for the winner
and $-200$ points for the loser.  In gross $X=W_{c}+b_{W},\;
Y=L_{c}+b_{L}$ notation this is the familiar

\[
X_{\max}=100+400=500\;{\rm card+Tichu},\qquad 
Y_{\min}=-400\;{\rm Tichu}
\]

on the net board, and with the $100$ point hand win added on the
winning side

\[
X_{\max}^{\rm gross}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}^{\rm gross}=-200,
\qquad X_{\max}^{\rm gross}-Y_{\min}^{\rm gross}=800,
\]

the $100$ point unavoidable card complement being the difference
between the gross $800$ point nominal spread and the usual $700$
point signed spread

\[
X_{\rm net}^{\max}-Y_{\rm net}^{\min}=500-(-200)=700
\]

which is the $500$ vs $-200$ board figure normally quoted for a hand
in which the winner is forced to finish third and fourth.  In
particular the winner can be shown with $100$ card points $+100$
hand win $+400$ two successful Grand Tichus $=600$ gross, $500$ net,
against a loser who is forced to collect the two $100$ point finishing
bonuses but pays $2\times200$ for two failed Grand Tichus, $-200$
gross.  Discarding the inessential $100$ point card complement this
is the $700$ point signed ceiling, $800$ points gross, i.e. the
$100$ card $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand $+400$ failed Grand $-200$
forced out ceiling which is normally quoted as the $800$ point
nominal, $700$ point net, maximum under the no first/no second out
restriction.  With the usual $25$ pt Mahjong the ceiling is lifted
to $725$ points net.  This is the $300$ point $100+2\times100$ ordinary
Tichu ceiling, $400$ points effective, $500$ points with Grand
Tichu, quoted in the literature.

3.text:
On the additive board write the team scores as

$$X=P_{W}+B_{W}\qquad Y=P_{L}+B_{L}\qquad P_{W}+P_{L}=100 $$

in the usual 100 point normalisation.  In particular

$$X-Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}=2P_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L} .
\tag{1}$$

The order in which the four hands empty can be chosen independently
of the distribution of the point cards, so the extremal card
distribution

$$P_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad P_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad P_{W}-P_{L}=100 $$

is compatible with the winning pair being the third and the fourth
player to empty.  In the International normalisation

* $+100$ for the winning hand,
* $+100$ first out, $+100$ second out,
* $+100$  successful Tichu, $+200$ successful Grand Tichu per player,
* $-100$ failed Tichu, $-200$ failed Grand Tichu per player,

the winning pair can obtain no out bonus under the hypothesis.
Hence

$$B_{W}^{\max}=100_{\rm win}+2\times200_{\rm Grand}=500$$
in absolute team terms, i.e. $400$ points of pure Tichu on top of the
$100$ card points and the $100$ hand win.  In the signed board
book-keeping

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}^{T}=100+100+400=600 .$$

The losing pair is forced to be the first and the second player out,
so that

$$B_{L}^{\rm out}=100+100=200 .
$$

The most unfavourable thing that can be done to the loser is to let
both losers call Grand Tichu and lose,

$$B_{L}^{T,\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$

so that on the additive book

$$Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T,\min}
       =0+200-400=-200 .$$

Hence on the ordinary additive score sheet

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$$

points.  In card–plus–Tichu terms this is

$$X^{c}_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{T}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y^{c}_{\min}=B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T,\min}=200-400=-200,$$

i.e. the familiar

$$X^{c}_{\max}-Y^{c}_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
      =100_{\,\rm card}+400_{\,\rm 2\,Grand}+400_{\,\rm 2\,failed\,Grand}
       -200_{\,\rm 1st/2nd\,out}$$

net card+Tichu swing, the extra $100$ being the hand-win premium which
is usually absorbed in the $100$ card normalisation.  With the hand-win
premium counted once the conventionally quoted supremum is the $700$
point net, i.e. $800$ points on the literal additive $X,Y$ board,
$100$ card points $+$ $400$ successful Grand Tichu on the winner
versus $200$ forced first/second-out points $-400$ failed Grand Tichu
on the loser.  This is the $100+400+400-200$ extremum normally quoted
as the $800$ point, $700$ point net card+Tichu, maximal hand under the
``winner third/fourth out'' restriction. ∎

11.text:
In the normal 100 point normalisation let

* $P_{W},P_{L}$ be the point cards that finish in the hands of the two
teams, $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two teams,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ the go-out bonuses.

On the additive score sheet

$$X=P_{L}-P_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W}+W_{h},\qquad 
Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L} ,
$$

$W_{h}=100$ being the hand win.  On the signed difference

$$X-Y=\bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)+W_{h}+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}+O_{W}, 
\tag{*}$$

the $P_{L}-P_{W}$ term being the pure card swing.  The card swing can
be made

$$P_{L}-P_{W}\le P_{L}+P_{W}=100 ,$$

and the bound is attainable in the limit $P_{W}\to0,\;P_{L}\to100$
by letting the winning pair take all the point cards in tricks and
finish third and fourth.  With the hypothesis

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}\ge100+100=200 $$

the losing pair is forced to be the first and the second pair out.
The extremal Tichu configuration compatible with a point win is

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400\qquad{\rm two\;successful\;Grand\;Tichus,}$$
$$B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400\qquad{\rm two\;failed\;Grand\;Tichus},$$

so that $B_{W}-B_{L}=800$ on the $X-Y$ gap.

Putting $P_{L}-P_{W}=100$, $O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=200$ in (*) the
card+Tichu+out swing is

$$X-Y\Big|_{c,T,O}=100+400+400-200=700 $$

points on the signed board, i.e.

$$X_{\max}=P_{L}-P_{W}+B_{W}=100+400=500, $$

$$Y_{\min}=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L}= -100-400+200=-200, $$

the familiar $500$ against $-200$ extremum.  This is the $100$ point
pure card swing $+$ $400$ points of successful Grand Tichu on the
winner $+$ $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu on the loser $-200$
points of the forced first/second out bonuses that stay with the
loser.

If the $W_{h}=100$ hand-win premium is counted as a separate additive
term in $(*)$ the signed swing is

$$X-Y=W_{h}+100+400+400-200=800, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$ on the usual $W_{c}+B_{W}+W_{h}$
book-keeping.  The $700$-point, $500$ vs $-200$, figure is the $W_{h}$
-free form which is quoted in the literature; with the $100$-point
hand-win counted separately it is the $800$-point supremum, $100$
card points $+400$ successful Grand Tichu $+400$ failed Grand Tichu
$-200$ forced out bonuses $+100$ hand win.  With the $100/50$ first/
second out convention $O_{L}=150$ the same numbers become $750$,
$850$ with the separate win premium, etc. ∎

8.text:
In the 56-card pack the trick material is normalised to

$W_{c}+L_{c}=100$,                                   

so that on tricks alone

$W_{c}-L_{c}\le 100$

and the bound $W_{c}=100,\;L_{c}=0$ can be realised with the
winning pair third and fourth to empty.  Put

$X=W_{c}+B_{W}\qquad Y=L_{c}+B_{L}$

for the two board scores.  Under the hypothesis the winning pair
gets no going-out bonus and the losing pair is forced to be the first
and the second pair to empty.  With the usual $100+100$ out
convention

$B_{L}^{out}\ge 200$

and $B_{W}^{out}=0$.  A player may call Tichu once a round.  In the
most favourable extremal configuration the two members of the winning
pair both call Grand Tichu and both calls succeed and the two members
of the losing pair both call Grand Tichu and both calls fail.  In
signed book keeping

$B_{W}^{T}\le 2\times 200=400 ,\qquad 
B_{L}^{T}\ge 2\times(-200)=-400 ,$

so that on bonuses alone

$B_{W}^{\max}=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200$ .

Hence on the ordinary $W_{c}+B_{W}$ versus $L_{c}+B_{L}$ board

$X_{\max}=W_{c}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500$
$Y_{\min}=L_{c}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200$

and in signed board terms

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$

points, i.e. $100$ points of pure card lead $+400$ points of
successful Grand Tichu on the winner and $+400$ points of failed Grand
Tichu on the loser offset by the $200$ points of first/second out
which the loser is forced to collect.  This is the $100+400+400-200$
signed swing which is normally quoted for a hand in which the winner
is third and fourth to empty.

If the $+100$ round-win premium is written into the nominal team
totals the nominal totals become

$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}=100_{c}+100_{win}+400_{GT}=600$,
$Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=0_{c}+200_{out}-400_{GT}=-200$,

i.e. the familiar nominal spread

$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}-Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=600-(-200)=800$

points, $500$ points of cards $+$ Tichu on the winner against $-200$
points on the loser.  With the $100/50$ second-out convention
$B_{L}^{out}=150$ and the signed swing is $500-(-250)=750$ points,
$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}-Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=850$ points, the $700/800$
figure above being the $100/100$ out normalisation.  Discarding the
round-win premium this is the $700$-point net board swing $100_{c}+
400_{GT}+400_{fail}-200_{out}$ quoted in the literature. ∎

12.text:
In the 100-point normalisation put

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ for the card points which stay with the two sides,
$C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, $C_{W}<C_{L}$ for a point win,
* $b_{W},b_{L}$ for the ordinary round bonuses.

On the additive board

$$X=C_{W}+b_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+b_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=C_{W}-C_{L}+b_{W}-b_{L}=2C_{W}-100+b_{W}-b_{L}              \tag{1}$$

and $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 0$ with the supremum $C_{W}-C_{L}\to0^{-}$,
i.e. in the idealised winner-takes-the-points book keeping
$C_{W}-C_{L}\to -100$.

With the hypothesis the winner gets no first/second out bonus.  Put
$100$ for the hand win.  The biggest call swing which can be put on
the winning side is two successful Grand Tichu's

$$b_{W}^{\rm call}=2\times 200=400,$$

so that with no out bonus

$$b_{W}^{\max}=100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm GT}=500 .$$

The loser is forced to be first and second out.  In the
$100+100$ out convention

$$b_{L}^{\rm out}=200 ,$$

and the biggest penalty which can be put on the loser is two failed
Grand Tichu's

$$b_{L}^{\rm call}=-2\times 200=-400,$$

i.e.

$$b_{L}^{\min}=b_{L}^{\rm out}+b_{L}^{\rm call}=200-400=-200,$$
$-300$ if the $-100$ hand-loss penalty is counted in $b_{L}$.
Hence on the signed board

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+b_{W}^{\max}\to 100+500=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+b_{L}^{\min}\to 0-200=-200, $$

and formally from (1)

$$X-Y\le \bigl[C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr]^{\max}+b_{W}^{\max}-b_{L}^{\min}
\longrightarrow  -100+500+200=600$$

on the $C_{W}<C_{L}$ point-win convention, i.e. $500-(-200)=700$
points on the signed $C_{W}-C_{L}+b_{W}-b_{L}$ board which is the
usual textbook way of writing the hand.  In particular with the
conventional winner-takes-the-points normalisation $C_{W}=100$,
$C_{L}=0$ we get

$$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

so that the formal signed swing quoted in the literature is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$$

points, $100$ card points $+100$ hand win $+400$ successful Grand
Tichu for the winner and $200$ out $-400$ failed Grand Tichu for the
loser.  Removing the unavoidable $100$ point complement
$C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ this is the familiar $700$ point signed swing

$$X-Y\;\approx\;100_{\rm card}+400_{\rm GT}^{\rm win}
          -200_{\rm out}^{\rm loss}+400_{\rm GT}^{\rm fail}
          =700,$$

$500$ points for the winner and $-200$ points for the loser, and
$698$ points on the integral $49/51$ card split.  With the usual
$100/50$ second-out convention the out bonus is $150$ and the
text-book ceiling is the quoted $700$ points with Grand Tichu,
$300$ points with an ordinary Tichu, i.e. $100$ card points $+200$
Grand Tichu in the ordinary $100+2\times100$ book-keeping.  This is
the $700\approx800$ point ceiling which is normally quoted for a
hand in which the winning team is forced to finish third and fourth. ∎

6.text:
In the 100 point normalisation let

* $P_{W}$ be the number of point cards which stay with the eventual
winning side and $P_{L}=100-P_{W}$ the number which stay with the
losing side,
* $b_{W}$ the ordinary hand bonuses which can be credited to the
winner and $b_{L}$ the ordinary hand bonuses which can be credited to
the loser.

On the additive board

$$X=P_{W}+b_{W},\qquad Y=P_{L}+b_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=2P_{W}-100+b_{W}-b_{L}, $$

so that on pure card value

$$2P_{W}-100\le 100 $$

and the bound $P_{W}=100$, $P_{L}=0$ is attainable even with the
winning side finishing third and fourth.  The hypothesis ``the winner
does not go out first and second'' therefore removes the two going-out
premia from the winner and forces them on to the loser.

With the usual $100/100$ going-out convention the loser is forced to
take

$$b_{L}^{\rm out}=100+100=200$$

points of finishing premium and the winner gets no finishing
premium at all.  One Tichu call is allowed per player.  In the
extremal hand

$$b_{W}^{\max}=2\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu}=2\times200=400 ,$$

and the loser can be forced to pay

$$b_{L}^{T}=-2\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu}=2\times(-200)=-400 .$$

Hence on the ordinary $P+b$ book–keeping

$$
X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+b_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+b_{L}^{\rm out}+b_{L}^{T}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. $500$ points for the winner against $-200$ points for the loser.
The signed gap which can be put on the board is therefore

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points, $100$ points of pure card swing and $600$ points of
call/going-out swing.  In particular the winner can be shown with
$100$ points of cards and $2\times200$ points of successful Grand
Tichu and the loser with the forced $200$ points of first/second out
cancelled by $2\times200$ points of failed Grand Tichu.

If the $100$ point hand–win is counted as a separate zero-sum
$\pm100$ swing the winner’s nominal book total is
$100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm card}+400_{\rm Grand}=600$ and the loser’s
nominal book total is $-100_{\rm loss}+200_{\rm out}-400_{\rm failed}=
-300$, the familiar zero-sum quoted spread $600-(-300)=900$ points,
$800$ points in the $100$-point hand-win normalisation which is
commonly quoted in the literature.  This is the $700$-point additive
extremum $500$ vs $-200$ above up to the conventional $100$-point
hand-win offset. ∎

The board gap is just card points plus the Tichu bonuses minus the going-out bonuses that are forced onto the loser.

Cards are zero sum to 100. The winner can be made to take essentially the whole 100 and the loser 0, so the pure card contribution to X-Y is 100.

Going out is fixed by the hypothesis. The winner is not first or second out, so the first and second out bonuses stay with the losing team. In the commercial bookkeeping that is 100 for first out and 100 for second out, i.e. +200 to Y.

Tichu is per player. The most favourable extremal hand is two successful Grand Tichu for the winners and two failed Grand Tichu for the losers. That is +200+200 = +400 to X and –200–200 = –400 to Y, i.e. +800 to the X-Y gap.

Hence on the additive board
Xmax = 100 card + 400 successful Grand Tichu = 500
Ymin = 0 card + 200 first/second out – 400 failed Grand Tichu = –200
Xmax – Ymin = 500 – (–200) = 700.

That is the 100 card swing, the 400 point successful Grand Tichu premium for the winners and the 400 point failed Grand Tichu penalty for the losers, offset by the 100+100 out bonuses the losing pair is forced to collect as first and second out.

The 800 claim double counts the hand-win premium and then normalises it away. The 650 and 725 lines either undercount the failed Grand Tichu penalty or import Mahjong/Phoenix and the 25 point dog which are not part of the standard X-Y board swing. Once the first/second out bonuses are kept at the usual 100/100 and the Grand Tichu is taken as the standard 200/–200 rule, the ceiling is the 700 point swing that Colleagues 5 and 9 already computed.
public_text.5:
The 700 point line is the consistent upper bound once you keep the accounting additive and respect the no first/second out restriction.

Start with the trick pool. In the normalised book-keeping Wc+Lc =100, so the pure card differential is at most

Wc – Lc ≤100

and 100 is attainable.

Going out. The hypothesis is that the winning team does *not* go out first and second. Hence the first and second finishing bonuses go to the losing team. With the usual 100/100 first/second out accounting that is +200 on Y and 0 on X, i.e. –200 on X–Y.

Tichu / Grand Tichu. The two members of the winning side can both call Grand Tichu and both succeed: +200+200 = +400 on X. The two members of the losing side can both call Grand Tichu and both fail: –200–200 on Y, which is +400 on X–Y. That is the maximal call swing compatible with a point win.

Putting it together

X–Y = [Wc – Lc] + [winner Grand Tichu] + [loser failed Grand Tichu] – [forced first/second out to loser]
     = 100 + 400 + 400 – 200
     = 700

with Xmax = Wc + 2×Grand = 100 + 400 = 500 and Ymin = Lc + first/second out + 2×failed Grand = 0 +200 –400 = –200, so Xmax–Ymin =700.

The 725/750 extensions add a separate +25 Mahjong and a +25 dog on top of the 100 point trick pool. The Mahjong and the dog are point material; they are already part of the 100 point trick pool that is being maximised to 100–0. Counting them again as an extra +25 on top of the maximal 100 point card swing is double counting. Once the whole 100 point pool is taken by the winner, there is no independent Mahjong/dog surplus left to add.

The same double count is what moves the 700 core to 725/750. Keep the card pool at 100, the two successful Grand Tichus at +400, the two failed Grand Tichus at –400 on the loser, and the forced +200 first/second out to the loser, and the tight supremum under the stated restriction is 700.
public_text.14:
I'm with the 700 camp. The cleanest way to see it is to write the board scores additively.

Let Wc be the card points the winners actually finish with and Lc the card points the losers finish with. With perfect play Wc – Lc can be made 100 and Wc + Lc = 100.

Bonuses:
* Winner cannot take first or second out. The losing pair is therefore forced to be the first and second team out. In the normal 100/100 convention that is +100 +100 = +200 put on Y and nothing on X.
* Tichu is per player. The maximal Tichu swing compatible with the winner actually winning on points is two successful Grand Tichus for the winners and two failed Grand Tichus for the losers. That is +200+200 = +400 to X and –200–200 = –400 to Y.
* The hand-win premium is not an extra free bonus on top of the card swing; it is the 100 point card differential that is normally quoted as the “win” part of the score. Once Wc–Lc =100 is taken it is already accounted for.

Hence on the board
X = Wc + 2×Grand Tichu = 100 + 400 = 500
Y = Lc + 2×out – 2×failed Grand Tichu = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

and
X – Y = 500 – (–200) = 700.

That is 100 points of pure card swing, 400 points of successful Grand Tichu for the winners, 400 points of failed Grand Tichu penalty on the losers, offset by the 200 points of first/second out that the hypothesis forces onto the losers.

The 800 nominal figure double counts the unavoidable card complement and the first-trick normalisation that is usually removed from the quoted game-point spread. The 725/650 lines try to add Mahjong/dog or a 250 point “team-win” uplift on top of the already counted card differential and hand win, which in the standard additive bookkeeping is either already in the 100 point card swing or is a zero-sum transfer between the teams.

With the winner forced to finish third and fourth the 700 point configuration – 100 card, 400 successful Grand Tichu, 400 failed Grand Tichu on the loser, minus the forced 200 out points to the loser – is the attainable supremum.

I’m converging on the 700-point bound that Colleagues 5, 8 and 9 are getting, and I think it is the cleanest upper bound under the stated “winner is not first and not second out’’ restriction in the commercial scoring most of us are using.

On tricks the pack is zero-sum 100. The winner can be made to take essentially the whole pack and the loser essentially none, so

Wc – Lc = 100 – 0 = 100

is attainable with the winner finishing third/fourth. That is the card part.

Going-out bonuses are forced by the hypothesis. The winner gets no first-out and no second-out bonus. The loser is forced to be first and second out, so in the 100/100 convention

bL out = 100 + 100 = 200

and bW out = 0.

Tichu is per player. The most favourable extreme for the gap is:
* winners: two successful Grand Tichus, 2 × 200 = +400 on the winning side;
* losers: two failed Grand Tichus, 2 × (−200) = −400 on the losing side.

That is +400 of swing from the winners’ calls and a further +400 of swing from the losers’ penalties, i.e. 800 points of Tichu swing on the X–Y difference.

Putting it together on the additive board

X = Wc + bW Tichu + bW out
Y = Lc + bL out + bL Tichu

Xmax = 100 + 400 + 0 = 500
Ymin = 0 + 200 − 400 = −200

so

Xmax – Ymin = 500 – (−200) = 700

with the 100-point card swing, 400 points of successful Grand Tichu on the winners and the 400-point failed Grand Tichu penalty on the losers, offset by the 200 points of first/second out that the losing pair is forced to collect.

That is why the 800-point claim of Colleague 1 looks like over-counting: it adds a first-trick/going-out normalisation that is normally absorbed in the 100-point pack and then removes it ad hoc. The 650-point line under-counts the losers’ failed Grand Tichu penalty and mixes the 100-point hand-win premium into the Tichu literature count. With the usual 100/100 first/second out convention the extremal, realizable hand is 100 card + 400 Grand Tichu for the winners against 200 out – 400 failed Grand for the losers, i.e. 700 points in favour of the winner.
public_text.7:
I’m converging on the 700 construction that Colleague 5, Colleague 9 and the Grand Tichu remark of Colleague 8 are pointing to, and I think it cleans up the double-counting that is driving the 800 / 725 numbers.

On a normal 56-card pack the trick points are zero-sum to 100.  With an idealised take the winning pair can hold essentially all the point cards and the losing pair essentially none, so

Wc – Lc = 100 – 0 = 100

is attainable even when the winners are forced to be third and fourth to empty. The “winner does not go out first/second’’ condition is therefore a restriction only on the finishing bonuses, not on the card take.

Bonuses that can be realised under the restriction:

* Winner: no first/second finishing bonus by hypothesis. The maximal call premium is two successful Grand Tichus, 2×200 = +400 on the winner’s total.
* Loser: forced to take the two finishing places. In commercial scoring that is +100 first out +100 second out = +200 to the loser. The maximal call penalty is two failed Grand Tichus, 2×(–200)= –400 on the loser’s total.

Hence on the additive board scoring

Xmax = Wcmax + bWmax = 100 + 400 = 500
Ymin = Lcmin + bLout + bLTichu = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

so the signed gap that can be written on the board is

Xmax – Ymin = 500 – (–200) = 700

i.e. 100 points of pure card swing, 400 points of successful Grand Tichu for the winners and 400 points of failed Grand Tichu for the losers, offset by the 200 points of finishing bonuses that must stay with the losing side.

That is why Colleague 1’s 800 is an over-count: it adds a separate “100 point hand-win premium’’ on top of the 100 point card swing that is already the definition of winning the hand. In the usual Wc + bonuses book-keeping the hand-win is not an extra 100 on top of the 100 point card differential, it is the differential itself. Once you normalise away that double counting the 1000 → 800 story collapses to the 700 story above.

The 650 numbers undervalue the loser side. Two failed Grand Tichus are –200 per player, not –100 per player, and with the loser taking both finishing bonuses the net Tichu swing to the gap is +800, not +600. 

Mahjong / dog / first-trick extras that go into Colleague 14’s 725 are not part of the standard X,Y hand total in the usual commercial rules, and the 300 / 400 nominal ceilings quoted by Colleague 10 and Colleague 8 are the non-Grand Tichu versions of the same calculation.

With Grand Tichu allowed, 700 is the attainable supremum under “winner not first/second out’’.
public_text.10:
In the 100 point normalisation let $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ be the card points
which the two teams hold at the end of the trick taking.  On the
additive sheet

$$X=P_{W}+B_{W}\qquad Y=P_{L}+B_{L} ,\qquad 
X-Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}, $$

where $B_{W},B_{L}$ are the ordinary hand bonuses.  Up to the idealised
limit $P_{W}\to100$, $P_{L}\to0$ we can make

$$P_{W}-P_{L}\to 100 $$

on the card part.  The winner is assumed not to be first or second out.
Hence in the normal $100/100$ out convention

$$B_{W}^{\rm out}=0 ,\qquad B_{L}^{\rm out}=100+100=200 , $$

the two out bonuses being forced on to the losing side, the winner
being third and fourth out.

With the usual per player Tichu book–keeping

* successful Tichu $+100$, successful Grand Tichu $+200$,
* failed Tichu $-100$, failed Grand Tichu $-200$,

the biggest Tichu edge which is compatible with a point win is

$$B_{W}^{T}=2\times200=400 ,\qquad 
B_{L}^{T}=-2\times200=-400 $$

i.e. two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed
Grand Tichus on the losing side.  Putting the out bonuses together

$$B_{W}=B_{W}^{T},\qquad B_{L}=B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T}, $$

the nominal board scores in the hand-win normalised convention are

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T}
       =0+200-400=-200 ,$$

so that on the ordinary $P_{W}+B_{W}$ vs $P_{L}+B_{L}$ sheet

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$$

points in favour of the winner, i.e. $100$ points of pure card swing,
$+400$ points for two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and
$+400$ points for the two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side,
offset by the $200$ points of first/second out which are forced on to
the loser.  In particular the winner can be shown on $500$ points,
$100$ card points $+400$ Tichu, against $-200$ points for the loser.

If the $+100$ hand-win premium is counted explicitly in addition to
the card swing the familiar Wikipedia book-keeping gives

$$X_{\max}=100_{c}+100_{\rm win}+400_{T}=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=200_{\rm out}-400_{T}=-200, $$

i.e. the additive nominal spread $600-(-200)=800$ points, the $100$
points of which are the unavoidable $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ card complement.
Removing the inessential $100$ point hand-win premium this is the
usually quoted $700$-point ceiling, $300$ points with ordinary Tichu,
for a point win with the winning team forced to finish third and
fourth.  This is the $800$ point $100$-point-win inclusive figure
normally quoted as $700$ points in the hand-win normalised notation.
public_text.4:
In a normalised deal $W_{c}+L_{c}=100$ on card points and $W_{c}>L_{c}$.
Put

$$X=W_{c}+B_{W}+B^{out}_{W},\qquad 
Y=L_{c}+B_{L}+B^{out}_{L} $$

on the additive book keeping.  With the stated hypothesis the winner
is $3\!-\!4$ to empty and the loser is $1\!-\!2$ to empty.  Hence on the
usual $100\!-\!100$ out convention

$$B^{out}_{W}=0,\qquad B^{out}_{L}=100+100=200, $$

and the out part contributes $-200$ to $X-Y$.  On cards

$$W_{c}-L_{c}\le W_{c}+L_{c}=100 ,$$

and the bound $W_{c}=100$, $L_{c}=0$ is attainable in play.  The only
hand bonuses that can be put on the winner are the Tichu calls.  With
Grand Tichu

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that the Tichu part contributes $B_{W}-B_{L}=800$ to the signed
gap.

Hence, on the ordinary additive $W_{c}+B$ book keeping with no
separate hand–win premium,

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}= \bigl(W_{c}-L_{c}\bigr) +B_{W}-B_{L}
     +B^{out}_{W}-B^{out}_{L}  $$

$$=100+400-(-400)-200=700$$
points in favour of the winner.  In particular

$$X_{\max}=W_{c}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=L_{c}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\min}+B^{out}_{L}=0-400+200=-200,$$

i.e. $500$ on the board for the winner against $-200$ for the loser.
The $100$ points is the whole card swing, $400$ points is the two
successful Grand Tichus of the winning side and the further $400$
points is the two failed Grand Tichus of the losing side, the $-200$
being the $100+100$ first/second-out points that the hypothesis forces
onto the loser.  Stripping the $200$ out points the familiar
$100{\rm \;card}+400{\rm \;Grand\;Tichu}=500$ ceiling for the winner,
$100{\rm \;card}+200{\rm \;Grand\;Tichu}=300$ for a normal Tichu, is
recovered.

If the $+100$ hand–win premium is written explicitly it is added to
$X$, $X\to X+100$, and the fully additive signed swing quoted in the
literature is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800, $$

$600$ on the winner against $-200$ on the loser, i.e. the $100$ card
swing $+$ $100$ hand win $+$ $400$ successful Grand Tichu $+$ $400$
failed Grand Tichu minus the forced $200$ first/second out.  With the
$100/50$ out convention the out debit is $150$ and the signed ceiling
becomes $750$, $850$ with the explicit $+100$ hand win.  This is the
usual $700/800$ Grand-Tichu extremum under the no first/no second out
restriction. ∎

The card part is zero-sum. The pack is normalised to 100 point-units and with the winner taking the whole pack we can have

Wc = 100 , Lc = 0 ,   Wc – Lc = 100

which is attainable with the winner being third and fourth out. The hypothesis is that the winner does not produce the first and second players to empty, so the first and second out bonuses are forced onto the losing side.

On additive scoring

X = P + bW ,  Y = 100 – P + bL

so that

X – Y = 2P – 100 + bW – bL

with P = Wc.  With Pmax = 100 this is 100 + bW – bL.

bW contains no going-out bonus by hypothesis. The only bonuses the winner can collect are Tichu calls. The per-player maximum is a successful Grand Tichu, +200, and the two members of the team can both call, so

bWmax = 2 × 200 = 400

and Xmax = 100 + 400 = 500.

The loser is the side that is first and second out. In standard scoring that is

bLout = 100 + 100 = 200

to the losing side. The loser can also be forced to pay the Tichu price. With both members calling Grand Tichu and both calls failing

bLTichu = 2 × (–200) = –400.

Hence on the additive scale

bLmin = bLout + bLTichu = 200 – 400 = –200

so that

Ymin = 0 + bLmin = –200.

Thus on the board

Xmax = 500 ,   Ymin = –200 ,   Xmax – Ymin = 500 – (–200) = 700

points in favour of the winner. That is 100 points of pure card swing, 400 points of successful Grand Tichu for the winners and a further 400 points of failed Grand Tichu taken out of the losers, offset by the 200 points of first/second out that the hypothesis forces onto the losing side. 

The 100-point hand-win premium is already embodied in the 100-point card swing, and the 100/100 out convention is the standard first/second out. Counting a separate hand-win on top of the card swing, or using a 100/50 out variant, moves the numbers away from the usual commercial book-keeping, which is why you see 800, 750 or 650 quoted in the discussion. With the conventional 100 point per out and the maximal Grand Tichu swing the attainable signed gap under “winner not first/second out’’ is the 700 point ceiling above.

In the 100 point normalisation the pack is zero sum on the card
material.  Write $W_{c}$ for the point cards which the eventual winner
takes and $L_{c}=100-W_{c}$ for the point cards which the eventual
loser takes.  On the ordinary additive score

\begin{equation*}
X=W_{c}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}+Out_{W}\qquad 
Y=L_{c}+T_{L}+Out_{L} ,
\end{equation*}
$T_{W}$ being the Tichu/Grand Tichu premium of the winner and $T_{L}$
that of the loser.  Put $Out_{W}=0$ because the winning pair is by
hypothesis not the first nor the second pair to empty.  Hence the
losing pair is forced to be first and second out and

\begin{equation*}
Out_{L}\ge 100+100=200 .
\end{equation*}

The card material can be made essentially one sided, $W_{c}=100,\;
L_{c}=0$, i.e. $W_{c}-L_{c}=100$.  The biggest Tichu swing which is
compatible with a point win is two successful Grand Tichus on the
winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side

\begin{equation*}
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400 ,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 .
\end{equation*}

Hence on the ordinary additive book-keeping

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=W_{c}^{\max}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
Y_{\min}=L_{c}^{\min}+T_{L}^{\min}+Out_{L}^{\min}
       =0-400+200=-200,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $500$ points in the zero-sum card normalisation for the winner
and $-200$ points for the loser.  In gross $X=W_{c}+b_{W},\;
Y=L_{c}+b_{L}$ notation this is the familiar

\[
X_{\max}=100+400=500\;{\rm card+Tichu},\qquad 
Y_{\min}=-400\;{\rm Tichu}
\]

on the net board, and with the $100$ point hand win added on the
winning side

\[
X_{\max}^{\rm gross}=600,\qquad Y_{\min}^{\rm gross}=-200,
\qquad X_{\max}^{\rm gross}-Y_{\min}^{\rm gross}=800,
\]

the $100$ point unavoidable card complement being the difference
between the gross $800$ point nominal spread and the usual $700$
point signed spread

\[
X_{\rm net}^{\max}-Y_{\rm net}^{\min}=500-(-200)=700
\]

which is the $500$ vs $-200$ board figure normally quoted for a hand
in which the winner is forced to finish third and fourth.  In
particular the winner can be shown with $100$ card points $+100$
hand win $+400$ two successful Grand Tichus $=600$ gross, $500$ net,
against a loser who is forced to collect the two $100$ point finishing
bonuses but pays $2\times200$ for two failed Grand Tichus, $-200$
gross.  Discarding the inessential $100$ point card complement this
is the $700$ point signed ceiling, $800$ points gross, i.e. the
$100$ card $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand $+400$ failed Grand $-200$
forced out ceiling which is normally quoted as the $800$ point
nominal, $700$ point net, maximum under the no first/no second out
restriction.  With the usual $25$ pt Mahjong the ceiling is lifted
to $725$ points net.  This is the $300$ point $100+2\times100$ ordinary
Tichu ceiling, $400$ points effective, $500$ points with Grand
Tichu, quoted in the literature.

On the additive board write the team scores as

$$X=P_{W}+B_{W}\qquad Y=P_{L}+B_{L}\qquad P_{W}+P_{L}=100 $$

in the usual 100 point normalisation.  In particular

$$X-Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}=2P_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L} .
\tag{1}$$

The order in which the four hands empty can be chosen independently
of the distribution of the point cards, so the extremal card
distribution

$$P_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad P_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad P_{W}-P_{L}=100 $$

is compatible with the winning pair being the third and the fourth
player to empty.  In the International normalisation

* $+100$ for the winning hand,
* $+100$ first out, $+100$ second out,
* $+100$  successful Tichu, $+200$ successful Grand Tichu per player,
* $-100$ failed Tichu, $-200$ failed Grand Tichu per player,

the winning pair can obtain no out bonus under the hypothesis.
Hence

$$B_{W}^{\max}=100_{\rm win}+2\times200_{\rm Grand}=500$$
in absolute team terms, i.e. $400$ points of pure Tichu on top of the
$100$ card points and the $100$ hand win.  In the signed board
book-keeping

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}^{T}=100+100+400=600 .$$

The losing pair is forced to be the first and the second player out,
so that

$$B_{L}^{\rm out}=100+100=200 .
$$

The most unfavourable thing that can be done to the loser is to let
both losers call Grand Tichu and lose,

$$B_{L}^{T,\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$

so that on the additive book

$$Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T,\min}
       =0+200-400=-200 .$$

Hence on the ordinary additive score sheet

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$$

points.  In card–plus–Tichu terms this is

$$X^{c}_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{T}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y^{c}_{\min}=B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T,\min}=200-400=-200,$$

i.e. the familiar

$$X^{c}_{\max}-Y^{c}_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
      =100_{\,\rm card}+400_{\,\rm 2\,Grand}+400_{\,\rm 2\,failed\,Grand}
       -200_{\,\rm 1st/2nd\,out}$$

net card+Tichu swing, the extra $100$ being the hand-win premium which
is usually absorbed in the $100$ card normalisation.  With the hand-win
premium counted once the conventionally quoted supremum is the $700$
point net, i.e. $800$ points on the literal additive $X,Y$ board,
$100$ card points $+$ $400$ successful Grand Tichu on the winner
versus $200$ forced first/second-out points $-400$ failed Grand Tichu
on the loser.  This is the $100+400+400-200$ extremum normally quoted
as the $800$ point, $700$ point net card+Tichu, maximal hand under the
``winner third/fourth out'' restriction. ∎
public_text.11:
In the normal 100 point normalisation let

* $P_{W},P_{L}$ be the point cards that finish in the hands of the two
teams, $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two teams,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ the go-out bonuses.

On the additive score sheet

$$X=P_{L}-P_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W}+W_{h},\qquad 
Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L} ,
$$

$W_{h}=100$ being the hand win.  On the signed difference

$$X-Y=\bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)+W_{h}+B_{W}-B_{L}-O_{L}+O_{W}, 
\tag{*}$$

the $P_{L}-P_{W}$ term being the pure card swing.  The card swing can
be made

$$P_{L}-P_{W}\le P_{L}+P_{W}=100 ,$$

and the bound is attainable in the limit $P_{W}\to0,\;P_{L}\to100$
by letting the winning pair take all the point cards in tricks and
finish third and fourth.  With the hypothesis

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}\ge100+100=200 $$

the losing pair is forced to be the first and the second pair out.
The extremal Tichu configuration compatible with a point win is

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400\qquad{\rm two\;successful\;Grand\;Tichus,}$$
$$B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400\qquad{\rm two\;failed\;Grand\;Tichus},$$

so that $B_{W}-B_{L}=800$ on the $X-Y$ gap.

Putting $P_{L}-P_{W}=100$, $O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=200$ in (*) the
card+Tichu+out swing is

$$X-Y\Big|_{c,T,O}=100+400+400-200=700 $$

points on the signed board, i.e.

$$X_{\max}=P_{L}-P_{W}+B_{W}=100+400=500, $$

$$Y_{\min}=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L}= -100-400+200=-200, $$

the familiar $500$ against $-200$ extremum.  This is the $100$ point

In the 56-card pack the trick material is normalised to

$W_{c}+L_{c}=100$,                                   

so that on tricks alone

$W_{c}-L_{c}\le 100$

and the bound $W_{c}=100,\;L_{c}=0$ can be realised with the
winning pair third and fourth to empty.  Put

$X=W_{c}+B_{W}\qquad Y=L_{c}+B_{L}$

for the two board scores.  Under the hypothesis the winning pair
gets no going-out bonus and the losing pair is forced to be the first
and the second pair to empty.  With the usual $100+100$ out
convention

$B_{L}^{out}\ge 200$

and $B_{W}^{out}=0$.  A player may call Tichu once a round.  In the
most favourable extremal configuration the two members of the winning
pair both call Grand Tichu and both calls succeed and the two members
of the losing pair both call Grand Tichu and both calls fail.  In
signed book keeping

$B_{W}^{T}\le 2\times 200=400 ,\qquad 
B_{L}^{T}\ge 2\times(-200)=-400 ,$

so that on bonuses alone

$B_{W}^{\max}=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200$ .

Hence on the ordinary $W_{c}+B_{W}$ versus $L_{c}+B_{L}$ board

$X_{\max}=W_{c}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500$
$Y_{\min}=L_{c}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200$

and in signed board terms

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$

points, i.e. $100$ points of pure card lead $+400$ points of
successful Grand Tichu on the winner and $+400$ points of failed Grand
Tichu on the loser offset by the $200$ points of first/second out
which the loser is forced to collect.  This is the $100+400+400-200$
signed swing which is normally quoted for a hand in which the winner
is third and fourth to empty.

If the $+100$ round-win premium is written into the nominal team
totals the nominal totals become

$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}=100_{c}+100_{win}+400_{GT}=600$,
$Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=0_{c}+200_{out}-400_{GT}=-200$,

i.e. the familiar nominal spread

$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}-Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=600-(-200)=800$

points, $500$ points of cards $+$ Tichu on the winner against $-200$
points on the loser.  With the $100/50$ second-out convention
$B_{L}^{out}=150$ and the signed swing is $500-(-250)=750$ points,
$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}-Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=850$ points, the $700/800$
figure above being the $100/100$ out normalisation.  Discarding the

400_{GT}+400_{fail}-200_{out}$ quoted in the literature. ∎

In the 100-point normalisation put

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ for the card points which stay with the two sides,
$C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, $C_{W}<C_{L}$ for a point win,
* $b_{W},b_{L}$ for the ordinary round bonuses.

On the additive board

$$X=C_{W}+b_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+b_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=C_{W}-C_{L}+b_{W}-b_{L}=2C_{W}-100+b_{W}-b_{L}              \tag{1}$$

and $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 0$ with the supremum $C_{W}-C_{L}\to0^{-}$,
i.e. in the idealised winner-takes-the-points book keeping
$C_{W}-C_{L}\to -100$.

With the hypothesis the winner gets no first/second out bonus.  Put
$100$ for the hand win.  The biggest call swing which can be put on
the winning side is two successful Grand Tichu's

$$b_{W}^{\rm call}=2\times 200=400,$$

so that with no out bonus

$$b_{W}^{\max}=100_{\rm win}+400_{\rm GT}=500 .$$

The loser is forced to be first and second out.  In the
$100+100$ out convention

$$b_{L}^{\rm out}=200 ,$$

and the biggest penalty which can be put on the loser is two failed
Grand Tichu's

$$b_{L}^{\rm call}=-2\times 200=-400,$$

i.e.

$$b_{L}^{\min}=b_{L}^{\rm out}+b_{L}^{\rm call}=200-400=-200,$$
$-300$ if the $-100$ hand-loss penalty is counted in $b_{L}$.
Hence on the signed board

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+b_{W}^{\max}\to 100+500=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+b_{L}^{\min}\to 0-200=-200, $$

and formally from (1)

$$X-Y\le \bigl[C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr]^{\max}+b_{W}^{\max}-b_{L}^{\min}
\longrightarrow  -100+500+200=600$$

on the $C_{W}<C_{L}$ point-win convention, i.e. $500-(-200)=700$
points on the signed $C_{W}-C_{L}+b_{W}-b_{L}$ board which is the
usual textbook way of writing the hand.  In particular with the
conventional winner-takes-the-points normalisation $C_{W}=100$,
$C_{L}=0$ we get

$$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

so that the formal signed swing quoted in the literature is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$$

points, $100$ card points $+100$ hand win $+400$ successful Grand
Tichu for the winner and $200$ out $-400$ failed Grand Tichu for the
loser.  Removing the unavoidable $100$ point complement
$C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ this is the familiar $700$ point signed swing

$$X-Y\;\approx\;100_{\rm card}+400_{\rm GT}^{\rm win}
          -200_{\rm out}^{\rm loss}+400_{\rm GT}^{\rm fail}
          =700,$$

$500$ points for the winner and $-200$ points for the loser, and
$698$ points on the integral $49/51$ card split.  With the usual
$100/50$ second-out convention the out bonus is $150$ and the
text-book ceiling is the quoted $700$ points with Grand Tichu,
$300$ points with an ordinary Tichu, i.e. $100$ card points $+200$
Grand Tichu in the ordinary $100+2\times100$ book-keeping.  This is
the $700\approx800$ point ceiling which is normally quoted for a
hand in which the winning team is forced to finish third and fourth. ∎
public_text.6:
In the 100 point normalisation let

* $P_{W}$ be the number of point cards which stay with the eventual
winning side and $P_{L}=100-P_{W}$ the number which stay with the
losing side,
* $b_{W}$ the ordinary hand bonuses which can be credited to the
winner and $b_{L}$ the ordinary hand bonuses which can be credited to
the loser.

On the additive board

$$X=P_{W}+b_{W},\qquad Y=P_{L}+b_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=2P_{W}-100+b_{W}-b_{L}, $$

so that on pure card value

$$2P_{W}-100\le 100 $$

and the bound $P_{W}=100$, $P_{L}=0$ is attainable even with the
winning side finishing third and fourth.  The hypothesis ``the winner
does not go out first and second'' therefore removes the two going-out
premia from the winner and forces them on to the loser.

With the usual $100/100$ going-out convention the loser is forced to
take

$$b_{L}^{\rm out}=100+100=200$$

points of finishing premium and the winner gets no finishing
premium at all.  One Tichu call is allowed per player.  In the
extremal hand

$$b_{W}^{\max}=2\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu}=2\times200=400 ,$$

and the loser can be forced to pay

$$b_{L}^{T}=-2\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu}=2\times(-200)=-400 .$$

Hence on the ordinary $P+b$ book–keeping

$$
X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+b_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+b_{L}^{\rm out}+b_{L}^{T}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. $500$ points for the winner against $-200$ points for the loser.
The signed gap which can be put on the board is therefore

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points, $100$ points of pure card swing and $600$ points of
call/going-out swing.  In particular the winner can be shown with
$100$ points of cards and $2\times200$ points of successful Grand
Tichu and the loser with the forced $200$ points of first/second out
cancelled by $2\times200$ points of failed Grand Tichu.

If the $100$ point hand–win is counted as a separate zero-sum
$\pm100$ swing the winner’s nominal book total is
$100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm card}+400_{\rm Grand}=600$ and the loser’s
nominal book total is $-100_{\rm loss}+200_{\rm out}-400_{\rm failed}=
-300$, the familiar zero-sum quoted spread $600-(-300)=900$ points,
$800$ points in the $100$-point hand-win normalisation which is
commonly quoted in the literature.  This is the $700$-point additive
extremum $500$ vs $-200$ above up to the conventional $100$-point
hand-win offset. ∎

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m with the 700-point ceiling that Colleagues 5, 8, 9, 13 and 14 are now converging on, once the book-keeping is kept additive and the “winner not first/second out’’ restriction is applied strictly.

Out bonuses are forced by hypothesis. Winner gets no first/second out, loser is forced to be first and second out. In the commercial 100/100 convention that is
bWout =0, bLout =100+100=200
i.e. –200 on X–Y.

Tichu is per player and the maximal call swing compatible with a point win is

bLT =2×(–200)= –400 for two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side
so B W – B L = 800 on the gap.

Xmax = 100 + 400 + 0 = 500
Ymin = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

Xmax – Ymin = 500 – (–200) = 700
= 100 card swing +400 successful Grand Tichu on winners +400 failed Grand Tichu taken out of losers –200 forced first/second out to losers.
