1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m with the 700 camp that Colleagues 5, 9, 13, 14 and 7 have laid out, and I think it is the clean ceiling under the stated restriction with the commercial scoring most of us are using.

Cards are zero sum to 100. With the winner forced to finish third and fourth we can still make the card take essentially one-sided: 
Wc – Lc → 100 with Wc →100, Lc →0. That is the whole card contribution to X–Y.

Going out is fixed by the hypothesis. Winner does not go out first or second, so the first and second out bonuses are forced onto the losing side. In standard commercial book-keeping that is 100 for first out and 100 for second out, i.e. +200 to Y and 0 to X. That is –200 on the X–Y gap.

Tichu is per player. The extremal call configuration compatible with a point win is two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side:

B_W^T max = 2 × 200 = +400 on X
B_L^T min = 2 × (–200) = –400 on Y

i.e. +800 to the X–Y gap from calls alone.

Additively:

Xmax = Wc max + B_W^T max = 100 + 400 = 500
Ymin = Lc min + B_L^out + B_L^T min = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

Xmax – Ymin = 500 – (–200) = 700

That is 100 points of pure card swing, +400 points for two successful Grand Tichus on the winners and +400 points of failed Grand Tichu taken out of the losers, offset by the forced 200 points of first/second out that stay with the loser.

The 800 figure that keeps reappearing is the gross book-keeping that adds a separate +100 hand-win premium on top of the 100 point card swing that already defines winning the hand. Once the card differential is normalised to 100 the hand win is already embodied there; counting it again double counts the win.

The 750/850 remarks that use a 100/50 first/second out convention are a house variant. The standard game as quoted in the commercial literature uses 100/100 for first and second out. With 100/100 the forced out debit on the loser is 200, not 150, and the signed ceiling stays at the 700 point net board, 500 vs –200, that is attainable with Wc=100, Lc=0, two successful Grand Tichus for the winners and two failed Grand Tichus for the losers, winner third/fourth out. That is the maximal X–Y under “winner does not go out first and second”.

In the 100-point normalisation let $P_{W}$ and $P_{L}$ be the card points
that finish with the winner and the loser, $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$,
and let $B_{W},B_{L}$ be the ordinary hand bonuses.  On the additive

$$
B_{W}^{T,\max}=2\times{\rm Grand}=2\times200=400 ,
\qquad

points in favour of the winner.  That is $100$ points of pure card

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$$

points in favour of the winner.  That is the $100$ point pure card
swing $+400$ points for two successful Grand Tichus on the winner
$+400$ points for the two failed Grand Tichus on the loser, offset by
the $200$ points of first/second out which are forced onto the losing
side.  In $P_{W}-P_{L}+b_{W}-b_{L}$ notation

$$X-Y= P_{W}-P_{L}+b_{W}-b_{L}\le100+400+400-200=700,$$

with equality in the $100\!-\!0$ card limit with the winner $3\!-\!4$
to empty.

Counting the $+100$ hand-win premium explicitly in addition to the
card swing this is the familiar nominal book-keeping

$$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}=100_{c}+100_{\rm win}+400_{T}=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=-200,$$

i.e. the $600$ vs $-200$ nominal spread $X_{\max}^{\rm nom}-Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=800$
points, the extra $100$ being the conventional hand-win premium which
is already absorbed in the $P_{W}-P_{L}=100$ card normalisation.  The
$700$ point $500$ vs $-200$ net figure is the $W_{h}$-free form normally
quoted as the $800$-point gross maximum for a hand in which the winning
team is forced to finish third and fourth. ∎

11.text:
In the $100$ point normalisation the card material is zero sum

$$P_{W}+P_{L}=100 ,\qquad P_{W}>P_{L}\ {\rm on\ a\ point\ win},$$

and on the additive board

$$X=P_{W}+B_{W}+O_{W},\qquad Y=P_{L}+B_{L}+O_{L}, 
\qquad X-Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L} .$$

The card differential can be made essentially one sided and it is
compatible with the winning pair being third and fourth to empty,

$$P_{W}^{\max }-P_{L}^{\min}=100-0=100, $$

and $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$.

With the hypothesis $O_{W}=0$ the first and second out bonuses are
forced on to the loser.  On the $100/100$ commercial convention

$$O_{L}^{\min}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}=0,$$

so that $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$ on the $X-Y$ gap.

One Tichu call is allowed per player.  The Tichu swing which is
compatible with a point win is

$$B_{W}^{T,\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{T,\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$

two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand
Tichus on the loser, i.e.

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=400-(-400)=800$$

on bonuses alone.

Hence on the ordinary $P+B+O$ board

$$
X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{T,\max}=100+400=500,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{T,\min}
       =0+200-400=-200,
$$

so that in signed board terms

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points in favour of the winner.  In decomposition

$$
X-Y = \underbrace{100}_{P_{W}-P_{L}}
     +\underbrace{400}_{2\;{\rm succ.\;Grand}}
     +\underbrace{400}_{2\;{\rm fail.\;Grand}}
     -\underbrace{200}_{1^{st}/2^{nd}\ {\rm out}}=700 ,
$$

i.e. $100$ points of pure card swing, $400$ points of successful Grand
Tichu for the winners and a further $400$ points of failed Grand Tichu
taken out of the losers, offset by the $200$ points of first/second
out which the hypothesis forces onto the losing side.  That is the
usual $500$ vs $-200$ board extremum, $300$ points with ordinary
Tichu.

If the $+100$ hand–win premium is written explicitly as a separate
additive term, $X\to X+100$, the nominal totals become

$$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}=100_{c}+100_{\rm win}+400_{GT}=600,
\qquad Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=200_{\rm out}-400_{GT}=-200,$$

i.e. the familiar nominal spread

$$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}-Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=600-(-200)=800
$$

points, $700$ points net once the unavoidable $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$
complement is absorbed in the card swing.  With the $100/50$ second
out convention the out debit is $150$ and the numbers become $750$
net, $850$ nominal, etc.

6.text:
In the 100 point normalisation let $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ be the trick
points which stay with the two teams and put

$$X=P_{W}+B_{W},\qquad Y=P_{L}+B_{L},\qquad X-Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L} .$$

The pure card swing can be made

$$P_{W}-P_{L}\to 100,\qquad P_{W}\to 100,\;P_{L}\to 0 $$

and the bound is attainable with the winning pair third and fourth
to empty.  With the hypothesis

$$B_{W}^{\rm out}=0,\qquad B_{L}^{\rm out}=100+100=200 $$

the two first/second out bonuses are forced on to the losing side.
With one call per player

$$B_{W}^{T}\le 2\,{\rm Grand}=2\times 200=400,$$
$$B_{L}^{T}\ge 2\,{\rm failed\;Grand}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$

and the Tichu swing is $B_{W}-B_{L}\le 800$.
Hence on the $P+B$ sheet

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T}
       =0+200-400=-200, $$

i.e. $100$ points of pure card swing, $+400$ points of two
successful Grand Tichus on the winner and $+400$ points of two failed
Grand Tichus on the loser, the $200$ points of first/second out being
forced on to the loser.  In signed board terms

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
      =100_{c}+400_{GT}^{\rm win}+400_{GT}^{\rm fail}-200_{\rm out} ,$$

the familiar $500\;{\rm vs}\;-200$ extremum.  With the usual
$+100$ hand–win written out separately the nominal totals are
$X_{\rm nom}^{\max}=100_{c}+100_{win}+400_{GT}=600$ and
$Y_{\rm nom}^{\min}=200_{\rm out}-400_{GT}=-200$, i.e. the
$600\;{\rm vs}\;-200$ gross spread $600-(-200)=800$ points which is
commonly quoted as the $800$ point, $700$ point net, maximal hand
under the winner third/fourth out restriction.  Removing the
inessential $100$ point hand–win normalisation this is the $700$
point signed ceiling, $300$ points with ordinary Tichu. ∎

12.text:
In the 100 point normalisation write

$P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ for the trick points and $X=P_{W}+B_{W}$,
$Y=P_{L}+B_{L}$ for the additive board scores.  Then

$$X-Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=2P_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}.$$

The card swing can be made one sided and it can be made one sided
with the winners third and fourth to empty.  In the idealised limit

$P_{W}^{\max}=100$, $P_{L}^{\min}=0$, $P_{W}-P_{L}=100$,

which is compatible with the hypothesis $O_{W}=0$.

Out.  With the commercial $100/100$ first/second out convention the
hypothesis forces the two finishing bonuses on to the loser,

$$B_{W}^{out}=0,\qquad B_{L}^{out}=100+100=200, $$

i.e. $-200$ on $X-Y$.

Tichu.  One call per player.  The extremal call configuration which is
compatible with a point win is

$$B_{W}^{T,\max}=2\times{\rm Grand}=2\times200=400,
\qquad 
B_{L}^{T,\min}=2\times{\rm failed\;Grand}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that on bonuses alone $B_{W}-B_{L}=400-(-400)=800$.
Hence on the $P+B$ board

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{T,\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{out}+B_{L}^{T,\min}
        =0+200-400=-200,$$

and on the signed board

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
      =100_{\rm card}+400_{\rm 2\,Grand}^{\rm win}
       +400_{\rm 2\,failed\,Grand}^{\rm loss}-200_{\rm out}.$$

That is $100$ points of pure card swing, $+400$ points of two
successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and a further $+400$
points of two failed Grand Tichus taken out of the losing side, offset
by the $200$ points of first/second out which the hypothesis forces
onto the loser.  In particular the winner can be shown on $500$ points
$100$ card $+400$ Tichu against $-200$ points for the loser.

If the $+100$ hand-win premium is written as a separate additive term
the nominal totals are $X_{\max}^{nom}=100_{c}+100_{win}+400_{T}=600$
and $Y_{\min}^{nom}=-200$, i.e. the familiar nominal spread

$$X_{\max}^{nom}-Y_{\min}^{nom}=600-(-200)=800, $$

the $100$ points of which are the unavoidable $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ card
complement.  Removing that inessential $100$ point hand-win offset
this is the $700$-point, $500$ vs $-200$, net ceiling normally quoted
for a point win with the winning team forced to finish third and
fourth, $300$ points with ordinary Tichu.  With the $100/50$ second
out convention the out debit is $150$ and the net ceiling is $750$,
$850$ nominal. ∎

10.text:
In the 100 point normalisation $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ let

$$X=P_{W}+B_{W}\qquad Y=P_{L}+B_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}=2P_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L}$$
be the additive board scores.  The card swing can be made essentially
one sided and it can be made with the winners third and fourth to
empty, so that in the idealised limit

$$P_{W}-P_{L}\to 100,\qquad P_{W}\to100,\;P_{L}\to0,$$

is attainable under the hypothesis

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200$$

on the normal $100/100$ first/second out convention.  The only
bonuses the winner can collect are Tichu calls.

* Largest call swing compatible with a point win is
$B_{W}^{T}=2\times{\rm Grand}=2\times200=400$ on the winning side and
$B_{L}^{T}=2\times(-{\rm Grand})=2\times(-200)=-400$ on the losing
side, i.e. $B_{W}-B_{L}=800$ on the $X-Y$ gap.

Hence on the ordinary $P+B$ sheet

$$B_{W}^{\max}=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T}=200-400=-200,$$

so that

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\min}=0-200=-200,$$

and in signed board terms

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
       =100_{\rm card}+400_{\rm 2\,Grand^{win}}+400_{\rm 2\,Grand^{fail}}
        -200_{\rm 1st/2nd\,out}.$$

That is $100$ points of pure card swing, $+400$ points for two
successful Grand Tichus on the winners and $+400$ points for the two
failed Grand Tichus taken out of the losers, offset by the $200$
points of first/second out which the hypothesis forces onto the losing
side.  In particular the winner can be shown on $500$ net points,

If the $+100$ hand-win premium is written explicitly in the nominal
team totals

$$X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}^{T}
      =100+100+400=600,
\qquad 
Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T}
      =-200, $$

the familiar gross book-keeping is

$$X^{\rm nom}_{\max}-Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=600-(-200)=800,$$

i.e. $100$ card $+100$ win $+400$ successful Grand Tichu for the
winner and $200$ forced out $-400$ failed Grand Tichu for the loser.
Removing the inessential $100$ point hand-win offset this is the
usual $700$ point net $500$ vs $-200$ ceiling, $300$ points with an
ordinary Tichu, quoted for a hand in which the winning team is forced
to finish third and fourth.  This is the $700$ point net, $800$ point
gross, extremum under the $100/100$ out convention.

8.text:
With the additive book keeping write

$$X=P_{W}+B_{W}\qquad Y=P_{L}+B_{L},\qquad P_{W}+P_{L}=100$$

for the card material and the ordinary hand bonuses.  On tricks
$P_{W}-P_{L}\to 100$ can be made with the winning pair third and
fourth to empty, so that the $100$ point card swing can be realised
under the

$O_{W}=0$

restriction.  In the $100/100$ out convention the restriction forces

$$O_{L}\ge 100+100=200 ,\qquad O_{W}=0 $$

on to the losing side.  Per player at most one Tichu call can be made.

\qquad

Tichus on the losers.  Hence on the $P+B$ sheet

       =0+200-400=-200, $$

points in favour of the winner, i.e. $100$ points of pure card swing,

I'm with the 700 ceiling that colleagues 5, 8, 9, 13 and 14 are now laying out, and it is the clean ceiling under the commercial bookkeeping that is being used here.

Write the board additively as X = P_W + B_W , Y = P_L + B_L with P_W + P_L = 100. Then
X – Y = P_W – P_L + B_W – B_L = 2P_W – 100 + B_W – B_L.

Card part. The zero-sum pack can be made essentially one-sided even with the winner finishing third and fourth. P_W = 100, P_L = 0 is attainable, so P_W – P_L = 100 and 2P_W – 100 = 100.

Going out. The hypothesis is winner not first and not second out. In the standard 100 / 100 first / second out convention that forces the first and second out bonuses onto the losing side:
B_W^out = 0,
B_L^out = 100 + 100 = 200,
i.e. –200 on X – Y.

Tichu. Per player once per hand. The maximal compatible call swing is two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side:
B_W^T,max = 2 × 200 = 400,
B_L^T,min = 2 × (–200) = –400.
Hence B_W – B_L = 400 – (–400) = 800 on the Tichu part.

Putting it together on the P + B sheet
X_max = P_W^max + B_W^T,max = 100 + 400 = 500,
Y_min = P_L^min + B_L^out + B_L^T,min = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200,
so
X_max – Y_min = 500 – (–200) = 700
= 100 card swing + 400 successful Grand Tichu for the winner + 400 failed Grand Tichu on the loser – 200 forced first/second out to the loser.

That is 100 card points + 400 Grand Tichu + 400 failed Grand – 200 out. The 800 nominal figure that keeps appearing is the same construction with the 100 point hand-win premium written separately on top of the 100 point card differential, i.e. a double count of the unavoidable P_W + P_L = 100 complement. Once the hand win is absorbed in the card normalisation the quoted spread is the 500 vs –200, i.e. 700 point net gap.

The 750 numbers that are being mentioned in passing are the 100/50 first/second out house variant. With O_L = 100 + 50 = 150 the out debit becomes –150 and the nominal swing becomes 100 + 800 – 150 = 750, 850 with the explicit hand-win premium. That is a genuine house rule, but it is not the standard 100/100 commercial first/second out convention used in the literature that gives the 700 point net, 800 point gross ceiling. Staying with the standard 100/100 out and the standard Grand Tichu 200/–200 rule, the attainable supremum under winner third/fourth out is the 700 point board gap, 500 for the winner against –200 for the loser.

In the 100-point normalisation let $P_{W}$ and $P_{L}$ be the card points
that finish with the winner and the loser, $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$,
and let $B_{W},B_{L}$ be the ordinary hand bonuses.  On the additive
board

$$X=P_{W}+B_{W},\qquad Y=P_{L}+B_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}\;,$$

so that on cards alone $P_{W}-P_{L}\le 100$ and the bound is attainable
with the winner $3-4$ to empty.  Put $P_{W}^{\max}=100,\;P_{L}^{\min}=0$.

The hypothesis $W$ not $1/2$ out gives on the commercial $100/100$ out
convention
$$
B_{W}^{\rm out}=0,\qquad B_{L}^{\rm out}=100+100=200,
$$
the two out bonuses being forced on to the losing side.

Tichu is per player.  The Tichu swing which is compatible with a point
win is

$$
B_{W}^{T,\max}=2\times{\rm Grand}=2\times200=400 ,
\qquad 
B_{L}^{T,\min}=2\times(-{\rm Grand})=2\times(-200)=-400 ,
$$

i.e. two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed
Grand Tichus on the losing side.  Hence on the $P+B$ sheet

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=B_{W}^{T,\max}=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T,\min}=200-400=-200 .
$$

In particular

$$
X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

so that on the ordinary card-plus-bonus board

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$
points in favour of the winner.  That is $100$ points of pure card
swing $+400$ points for two successful Grand Tichus on the winners
$+400$ points for the two failed Grand Tichus on the losers $-$ the
$200$ points of first/second out which the hypothesis forces onto the
losing side.

If the $+100$ hand-win premium is written as a separate additive term
on top of the card differential the nominal totals become

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm nom}=100_{c}+100_{\rm win}+400_{GT}=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=200_{\rm out}-400_{GT}=-200,
$$

i.e. the familiar nominal spread $600-(-200)=800$, the $100$ points of
which are the unavoidable $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ card complement. Removing
that inessential hand-win offset this is the usual $700$-point,
$500$ vs $-200$, net ceiling, $100_{card}+400_{GT}^{win}+400_{GT}^{fail}
-200_{forced\;out}$, quoted for a hand in which the winning team is
forced to finish third and fourth.  With the $100/50$ out convention
this is $750$ net, $850$ nominal, and so on. ∎

reflection_text.6:
The pack is normalised to 100 point units, $P_W+P_L=100$. Card swing $P_W-P_L\le 100$ and attainable even with winner forced third/fourth to empty. Additive bookkeeping $X=P_W+b_W$, $Y=P_L+b_L$, $X-Y =2P_W-100+b_W-b_L$.

With winner not first/second out, $O_W=0$ and forced $O_L=100+100=200$ in standard 100/100 first/second out convention. Winner can collect Tichu only.

$B_W^{T,max}=2\times Grand =400$, $B_L^{T,min}=2\times(-Grand)=-400$.
Hence $B_W-B_L=800$.

On $P+B$ sheet:
$X_{max}=P_W^{max}+B_W^{T,max}=100+400=500$
$Y_{min}=P_L^{min}+O_L+B_L^{T,min}=0+200-400=-200$
$X_{max}-Y_{min}=500-(-200)=700 =100_{card}+400_{2\,succ\,Grand}+400_{2\,fail\,Grand}-200_{forced\;out}$.

If the +100 hand-win is written as a separate explicit term, $X^{nom}_{max}=100_c+100_{win}+400=600$, $Y^{nom}_{min}=-200$, nominal spread $600-(-200)=800$. The 800 figure is the usual literature gross quote; the 700 figure is the net signed $P+B$ spread with the hand win absorbed in the card differential.

Current round consensus: Colleagues 1,10,11,12,13,14,5,8,9 converged to 700 net / 800 gross under 100/100 out. Disagreement/variant notes:
- 100/50 second-out house variant gives $O_L=150$, net $750$, nominal $850$.
- 650/725 lines come from under-counting failed Grand as -100 not -200 or adding Mahjong/dog +25 on top of an already maximised 100-point pool, i.e. double counting.
- Some early claims of 800/650 etc. resolved.

Under the problem statement as normally interpreted with standard commercial additive scoring, 100/100 out, Grand Tichu allowed, winner forced third/fourth, the tight signed supremum is 700 points, 500 vs -200; the widely quoted gross figure is 800 points with explicit hand-win.

Unresolved: precise wording of X,Y definition in the question. If hand-win is counted separately, answer is 800; if strictly $X=P_W+b_W$, answer is 700. Best estimate for stated problem is 700 net, 800 gross.
reflection_text.3:
The card material is zero-sum to 100 in the normalisation. $P_W+P_L=100$, $P_W-P_L\le100$ and $P_W=100,P_L=0$ is realizable even with the winning team finishing third and fourth, so order of emptying is independent of point distribution.

Additive bookkeeping $X=P_W+B_W$, $Y=P_L+B_L$, $X-Y=2P_W-100+B_W-B_L$. Under the stated restriction $O_W=0$ and the first/second out bonuses are forced onto the loser.

Standard commercial $100/100$ first/second out:
$B_W^{out}=0$, $B_L^{out}=200$, i.e. $-200$ on $X-Y$.

Tichu is per player. Max call swing compatible with a point win is
$B_W^{T,max}=2\times Grand =2\times200=400$,
$B_L^{T,min}=2\times(-Grand)=2\times(-200)=-400$,
so $B_W-B_L=800$ on bonuses.

Hence on the usual $P+B$ sheet
$X_{max}=P_W^{max}+B_W^{T,max}=100+400=500$,
$Y_{min}=P_L^{min}+B_L^{out}+B_L^{T,min}=0+200-400=-200$,
$X_{max}-Y_{min}=500-(-200)=700$
$=100_{card}+400_{2\,succ\,Grand}+400_{2\,fail\,Grand}-200_{forced\;1st/2nd\;out}$.

This is the $500$ vs $-200$ net board ceiling. If the $+100$ hand-win premium is written explicitly on top of the $100$ card differential, the nominal totals become
$X_{nom}^{max}=100_c+100_{win}+400_T=600$, $Y_{nom}^{min}=-200$,
nominal spread $600-(-200)=800$, the extra $100$ being the unavoidable $P_W+P_L=100$ complement already absorbed in the $P_W-P_L$ swing.

Disagreements now resolved:
* $650/725$ lines undercount failed Grand penalty or add Mahjong/dog on top of the already maximal $100$ point pool.
* $750/850$ numbers correspond to the $100/50$ second-out house variant $O_L=150$ instead of $200$.
* $800$ figure is the gross book-keeping with explicit hand-win; $700$ is the net $P+B$ form.

Unresolved normative choice: whether $X,Y$ are defined to include a separate $+100$ hand-win premium in addition to the card swing. Under the usual $P+B$ commercial bookkeeping the clean supremum under “winner not first/second out’’ is $700$ points, $500$ vs $-200$, i.e. $800$ points gross with the explicit hand-win premium. Consensus in rounds 1-2 is 700 net /800 gross, with 700 being the standard quoted signed ceiling for $100/100$ out.

Going out under the standard commercial 100/100 convention is forced onto the loser by the hypothesis:
B_W^out =0, B_L^out =100+100=200 → -200 on X-Y.

Tichu per player. The extremal call configuration compatible with a point win is
B_W^T max =2×Grand =2×200 =+400
B_L^T min =2×failed Grand =2×(-200) =-400
so B_W-B_L =800 on bonuses.

Hence on the P+B sheet
X_max = Pc_max + B_W^T max =100+400=500
Y_min = Pl_min + B_L^out + B_L^T min =0+200-400=-200
X_max - Y_min =500-(-200)=700
=100_card +400_2succ Grand +400_2fail Grand -200_forced 1st/2nd out.

That is 100 points pure card swing, +400 successful Grand Tichu for the winners and +400 points taken out of the losers by two failed Grand Tichus, offset by the 200 points of first/second out forced on the loser.

If the +100 hand-win premium is written explicitly on top of the 100-point card differential, the nominal totals become
X_nom_max =100_c+100_win+400_T=600
Y_nom_min =200_out-400_T=-200
X_nom_max - Y_nom_min =800
the extra 100 being the inessential hand-win complement already embodied in Pc-Pl=100.

The 800 figure repeatedly quoted is therefore the same 700 net board with the hand win double-counted. The 750/850 numbers correspond to the 100/50 second-out house variant, B_L^out=150, giving net 750, nominal 850. The 650/725 lines earlier came from under-counting failed Grand Tichu, counting only ordinary Tichu, or trying to add Mahjong/dog on top of a pack already maximised to 100-0.

Current belief: under standard 100/100 first/second out, Grand Tichu allowed, winner forced third/fourth, the attainable supremum is the 500 vs -200 board, i.e. 700 points signed gap. Gross nominal with an explicit +100 hand-win term is 800. The consensus of Colleagues 1,5,8,10,11,12,13,14 in round 2 supports this 700 net / 800 gross ceiling, with the 100/50 variant noted as a house rule. Unresolved remains only the convention about whether X,Y are defined with an explicit separate hand-win premium; under the usual additive P+B definition the tight realizable supremum is 700.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m joining the 700 camp that Colleagues 1, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and others have now laid out. With the commercial additive book-keeping that is normally used it is the tight signed ceiling under the stated “winner does not go out first and second” restriction.

With the pack normalised to 100, P_W+P_L=100. The card swing can be made essentially one-sided and it is compatible with the winners finishing third and fourth:

P_W – P_L → 100, P_W → 100, P_L → 0

That 100 is the whole card contribution to X–Y; the hand win is already embodied in the P_W+P_L=100 normalisation.

Going out is forced by hypothesis. Winner gets no first/second out bonus:

O_W = 0, O_L = 100+100 = 200

on the standard 100/100 first/second out convention. That is –200 on the X–Y gap.

Tichu is per player. The extremal call configuration compatible with a point win is two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side:

B_W^Tmax = 2×200 = +400
B_L^Tmin = 2×(–200) = –400

i.e. +800 on the bonus differential.

Hence on the ordinary P+B board

Xmax = P_Wmax + B_W^Tmax = 100 + 400 = 500
Ymin = P_Lmin + O_L + B_L^Tmin = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

and in signed terms

Xmax – Ymin = 500 – (–200) = 700

= 100_card + 400_2 succ Grand + 400_2 fail Grand – 200_forced 1st/2nd out.

That is the textbook 500 vs –200 board extremum, 300 points with ordinary Tichu.

The 800 nominal numbers that keep appearing are the same construction with a separate +100 hand-win premium written on top of the 100 point card differential that already defines winning the hand. Once the hand win is absorbed in P_W–P_L=100 the gross 600 vs –200, i.e. 800 nominal, collapses to the 500 vs –200 signed 700 point ceiling.

The 750/850 remarks are the 100/50 second-out house variant, O_L=150 instead of 200. That is a recognised club variation, not the standard 100/100 first/second out convention used in the commercial literature. Under 100/50 you do get 750 net, 850 nominal, but with the standard 100/100 out the forced out debit is 200 and the signed ceiling stays at 700.

Mahjong/dog is also already inside the 100 point trick pool. Once P_W–P_L is taken to 100–0 there is no independent surplus left to add.

So with Grand Tichu allowed, winner forced third/fourth, standard 100/100 out, the attainable supremum is 100+400+400–200 = 700 points in favour of the winner.

6.text:
With the pack normalised to $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ put on the additive
$P+B$ sheet

$$X=P_{W}+B_{W},\qquad Y=P_{L}+B_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}$$
and $P_{W}-P_{L}\to100$ can be made with the winning pair third and
fourth to empty.  In the commercial $100/100$ first/second out
convention the hypothesis $O_{W}=0$ forces

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200$$
on to the losing side, i.e. $-200$ on $X-Y$.

One Tichu call per player.  The point–win compatible extremum is
two successful Grand Tichus on the winner and two failed Grand Tichus
on the loser,

$$B_{W}^{T,\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad
B_{L}^{T,\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that $B_{W}-B_{L}=800$ on bonuses alone.  Hence on the ordinary
$P+B+O$ board

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{T,\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+O_{L}+B_{L}^{T,\min}=0+200-400=-200,$$

and in signed board terms

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
      =100_{P_{W}-P_{L}}+400_{2{\rm succ.\,Grand}}+400_{2{\rm fail.\,Grand}}
       -200_{1st/2nd\,out}$$

i.e. $100$ points of pure card swing, $+400$ points for two successful
Grand Tichus on the winners and a further $+400$ points taken out of
the losers by two failed Grand Tichus, offset by the $200$ points of
first/second out which the hypothesis forces onto the losing side.
That is the usual $500$ vs $-200$ board extremum, $300$ points with
ordinary Tichu.

If the $+100$ hand–win premium is written explicitly as a separate
additive term $X^{\rm nom}=X+100$,

$$X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=100_{c}+100_{win}+400_{GT}=600,\qquad
Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-200,$$

the familiar nominal book-keeping is $X^{\rm nom}_{\max}-Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}
=600-(-200)=800$, the extra $100$ being the unavoidable
$P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ complement which is already absorbed in the
$P_{W}-P_{L}=100$ card swing.  Removing the inessential hand-win
double count this is the $700$ point net, $500$ vs $-200$, ceiling
normally quoted for a hand with the winning team forced to finish
third and fourth under the standard $100/100$ out convention.  On a
$100/50$ second-out house variant $O_{L}=150$ the signed ceiling is
$750$ net, $850$ nominal. ∎

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m joining the 700 net ceiling that Colleagues 1, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and others have now reconstructed, because it is the tight supremum under the commercial 100/100 first/second out book-keeping that is being used here.

On the additive sheet X = P_W + B_W, Y = P_L + B_L with P_W + P_L = 100. The card material can be made essentially one sided even with the winning pair finishing third and fourth to empty, so P_W - P_L → 100 is attainable with P_W → 100, P_L → 0.

The hypothesis forces the finishing bonuses. Winner does not go out first or second, so O_W = 0 and the first and second out bonuses are forced onto the loser. On the standard commercial convention that is 100 for first out and 100 for second out:

O_L = 100 + 100 = 200, O_W - O_L = -200 on X-Y.

Tichu is per player. The extremal call configuration compatible with a point win is two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side:

B_W^T,max = 2 × 200 = +400
B_L^T,min = 2 × (-200) = -400

i.e. B_W - B_L = 800 on bonuses alone.

Hence on the ordinary P+B board

X_max = P_W^max + B_W^T,max = 100 + 400 = 500
Y_min = P_L^min + O_L + B_L^T,min = 0 + 200 - 400 = -200

so in signed board terms

X_max - Y_min = 500 - (-200) = 700
= 100_card + 400_2 succ Grand + 400_2 fail Grand - 200_forced 1st/2nd out.

That is 100 points of pure card swing, +400 points for two successful Grand Tichus on the winners and +400 points of failed Grand Tichu taken out of the losers, offset by the 200 points of first/second out which the hypothesis forces onto the losing side. The 500 vs -200 board is attainable with Wc = 100, Lc = 0, two successful Grand Tichus for the winners and two failed Grand Tichus for the losers, winner third/fourth out.

The 800 nominal figures that keep appearing are the same construction with the +100 hand-win premium written explicitly on top of the 100 point card differential that is already embodied in P_W - P_L = 100. In the P+B normalisation the hand win is the card differential itself, so counting it again is double counting.

The 750/850 numbers mentioned in passing are the 100/50 second-out house variant. With O_L = 100 + 50 = 150 the out debit becomes -150 and the signed ceiling becomes 750 net, 850 nominal with the explicit win premium. That is a legitimate house rule, but it is not the standard 100/100 first/second out convention used in the commercial literature that the question refers to. Staying with the standard 100/100 out, the forced out debit is 200 and the attainable supremum under winner not first/second out is the 700 point net gap, 500 for the winner against -200 for the loser.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I am now fully with the 700 net, 500 vs –200 camp that Colleagues 5, 8, 9, 13 and 14 have laid out, and I think it is the clean ceiling under the commercial scoring that the question refers to.

With the pack normalised to 100, P_W+P_L = 100, and on the additive board X = P_W + B_W , Y = P_L + B_L

X – Y = P_W – P_L + B_W – B_L = 2P_W – 100 + B_W – B_L.

The card swing can be made essentially one sided and it is compatible with the winning pair finishing third and fourth to empty. In the idealised limit

P_W – P_L → 100, P_W →100, P_L →0

is attainable under the hypothesis O_W = 0.

Going out is fixed by the hypothesis. Winner does not go out first or second, so the first and second out bonuses are forced onto the losing side. In standard commercial book-keeping that is 100 for first out and 100 for second out,

B_W^out = 0, B_L^out = 100+100 = 200,

i.e. –200 on the X–Y gap. This is the 100/100 first/second out convention used in the commercial literature; the 100/50 second out remark is a recognised house variant, not the standard game as quoted.

Tichu is per player. The extremal call configuration compatible with a point win is two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side:

B_W^T max = 2 × 200 = +400 on X
B_L^T min = 2 × (–200) = –400 on Y

i.e. +800 to the X–Y gap from calls alone.

Additively on the P+B sheet

X_max = P_W^max + B_W^T max = 100 + 400 = 500
Y_min = P_L^min + B_L^out + B_L^T min = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

so

X_max – Y_min = 500 – (–200) = 700
= 100_card + 400_2 Grand win + 400_2 Grand fail – 200_1st/2nd out.

That is 100 points of pure card swing, +400 points for two successful Grand Tichus on the winners and +400 points of failed Grand Tichu taken out of the losers, offset by the forced 200 points of first/second out that stay with the loser. The winner can be shown on 500 net points, 100 card + 400 Tichu, against –200 points for the loser.

The 800 figure that keeps reappearing is the gross book-keeping that adds a separate +100 hand-win premium on top of the 100 point card swing that already defines winning the hand. Once the card differential is normalised to P_W+P_L=100 the hand win is already embodied there; counting it again double counts the win. In nominal terms that is X_nom max = 100_c + 100_win + 400_T = 600 vs Y_min = –200, i.e. the familiar 800 gross spread, which is 700 net once the unavoidable 100 point complement is absorbed.

The 750/850 remarks require O_L = 100+50 = 150, i.e. a 100/50 second out convention. With that house rule the out debit becomes –150 and you do get 750 net, 850 nominal. That is a genuine variant, but it is not the standard 100/100 out convention used in the standard game of Tichu. With the standard 100/100 out the forced out debit is 200 and the signed ceiling stays at the 700 point net board, 500 vs –200, attainable with Wc=100, Lc=0, two successful Grand Tichus for the winners and two failed Grand Tichus for the losers, winner third/fourth out.

For the stated restriction “winner does not go out first and second” under standard commercial scoring the supremum is therefore the textbook 500 vs –200, i.e. 700 points in favour of the winner.

i.e. $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$ on $X-Y$.

One Tichu call per player.  The point win compatible extremum is

$$B_{W}^{T,\max}=2\;{\rm Grand}=2\times 200=400,\qquad
B_{L}^{T,\min}=2\;{\rm failed\;Grand}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$

i.e. $B_{W}-B_{L}=800$ on Tichu alone.  Hence on the $P+B$ sheet

$$B_{W}^{\max}=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=O_{L}+B_{L}^{T,\min}=200-400=-200,$$

and

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
\qquad
Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\min}=0-200=-200,$$

so that in signed board terms

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
   =100_{P_{W}-P_{L}}+400_{2\,{\rm succ\;Grand}}
    +400_{2\,{\rm fail\;Grand}}-200_{1st/2nd\,out}$$

points in favour of the winner.  That is $100$ points of pure card
swing, $+400$ points for two successful Grand Tichus on the winning
side and a further $+400$ points taken out of the losers by two failed
Grand Tichus, offset by the $200$ points of first/second out which the
hypothesis forces onto the losing side.  In particular the winner can
be shown on $500$ net points, $100$ card $+400$ Tichu, against $-200$
points for the loser.

Writing the $+100$ hand–win premium explicitly as a separate additive
term, $X^{\rm nom}=X+100$, gives the familiar nominal book keeping

$$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}=100_{c}+100_{win}+400_{T}=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=-200,$$

i.e. the $600$ vs $-200$ nominal spread

$$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}-Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=600-(-200)=800,$$

the extra $100$ being the unavoidable $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ card complement
which is already absorbed in the $P_{W}-P_{L}=100$ swing above.  Removing
that inessential double count this is the usual $700$-point net,
$500$ vs $-200$, $100_{card}+400_{GT}^{win}+400_{GT}^{fail}-200_{out}$
ceiling for a hand in which the winning team is forced to finish
third and fourth, $300$ points with ordinary Tichu.  With the $100/50$
second out house variant $O_{L}=150$ the numbers become $750$ net,
$850$ nominal. ∎

8.text:
With the $100$ point normalisation put

$$P_{W}+P_{L}=100,\qquad X=P_{W}+B_{W},\;Y=P_{L}+B_{L},$$

so that on the ordinary $P+B$ sheet

$$X-Y=P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}=2P_{W}-100+B_{W}-B_{L} .$$

The pack can be made essentially one sided and the one sided limit is
compatible with the winners being $3-4$ to empty,

$$P_{W}^{\max }-P_{L}^{\min}=100-0=100 ,\qquad P_{W}^{\max}=100,\;
P_{L}^{\min}=0,$$

which is the whole card swing that can be realised under
$O_{W}=0$.

On the commercial $100/100$ first/second out convention the hypothesis
$W$ not $1/2$ out forces the two finishing bonuses on to the loser

$$B_{W}^{\rm out}=0,\qquad B_{L}^{\rm out}=100+100=200, $$

i.e. $-200$ on $X-Y$.

One Tichu call per player.  The point win compatible extremum is
two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand
Tichus on the losing side,

$$B_{W}^{T,\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad 
 B_{L}^{T,\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that on bonuses alone $B_{W}-B_{L}=400-(-400)=800$.

Hence on the $P+B$ board

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}^{T,\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}^{\rm out}+B_{L}^{T,\min}
        =0+200-400=-200,$$

and in signed board terms

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
   =100_{P_{W}-P_{L}}+400_{2\,{\rm succ}\,{\rm Grand}}
    +400_{2\,{\rm fail}\,{\rm Grand}}-200_{1^{st}/2^{nd}\,{\rm out}}.$$

That is $100$ points of pure card swing, $+400$ points for two
successful Grand Tichus on the winners and a further $+400$ points
taken out of the losers by two failed Grand Tichus, offset by the
$200$ points of first/second out which the hypothesis forces onto the
losing side.  In particular the winner can be shown $500=100_{c}+
400_{T}$ against $-200=200_{\rm out}-400_{T}$.

If the $+100$ hand-win premium is written explicitly on top of the
$P_{W}-P_{L}=100$ card differential the nominal totals are

$$X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=100_{c}+100_{\rm win}+400_{T}=600,\qquad
Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=200_{\rm out}-400_{T}=-200,$$

i.e. the familiar $600$ vs $-200$ gross book-keeping

$$X^{\rm nom}_{\max}-Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=600-(-200)=800,$$

the extra $100$ being the inessential hand-win complement already
embodied in $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$.  Removing that double count the
$P+B$ signed ceiling is the textbook $500$ vs $-200$, $700$ points in
favour of the winner, $300$ points with ordinary Tichu.  With the
common $100/50$ second-out house variant $B_{L}^{\rm out}=150$ the
signed ceiling becomes $750$, $850$ nominal. ∎

I’m joining the 700 camp that Colleagues 1, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and others have now laid out. With the commercial additive book-keeping that is normally used it is the tight signed ceiling under the stated “winner does not go out first and second” restriction.

With the pack normalised to 100, P_W+P_L=100. The card swing can be made essentially one-sided and it is compatible with the winners finishing third and fourth:

P_W – P_L → 100, P_W → 100, P_L → 0

That 100 is the whole card contribution to X–Y; the hand win is already embodied in the P_W+P_L=100 normalisation.

Going out is forced by hypothesis. Winner gets no first/second out bonus:

O_W = 0, O_L = 100+100 = 200

on the standard 100/100 first/second out convention. That is –200 on the X–Y gap.

Tichu is per player. The extremal call configuration compatible with a point win is two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side:

B_W^Tmax = 2×200 = +400
B_L^Tmin = 2×(–200) = –400

i.e. +800 on the bonus differential.

Hence on the ordinary P+B board

Xmax = P_Wmax + B_W^Tmax = 100 + 400 = 500
Ymin = P_Lmin + O_L + B_L^Tmin = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

and in signed terms

Xmax – Ymin = 500 – (–200) = 700

= 100_card + 400_2 succ Grand + 400_2 fail Grand – 200_forced 1st/2nd out.

That is the textbook 500 vs –200 board extremum, 300 points with ordinary Tichu.

The 800 nominal numbers that keep appearing are the same construction with a separate +100 hand-win premium written on top of the 100 point card differential that already defines winning the hand. Once the hand win is absorbed in P_W–P_L=100 the gross 600 vs –200, i.e. 800 nominal, collapses to the 500 vs –200 signed 700 point ceiling.

The 750/850 remarks are the 100/50 second-out house variant, O_L=150 instead of 200. That is a recognised club variation, not the standard 100/100 first/second out convention used in the commercial literature. Under 100/50 you do get 750 net, 850 nominal, but with the standard 100/100 out the forced out debit is 200 and the signed ceiling stays at 700.

Mahjong/dog is also already inside the 100 point trick pool. Once P_W–P_L is taken to 100–0 there is no independent surplus left to add.

So with Grand Tichu allowed, winner forced third/fourth, standard 100/100 out, the attainable supremum is 100+400+400–200 = 700 points in favour of the winner.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I'm joining the 700 net ceiling that has now been reconstructed by Colleagues 1, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 4.

On the ordinary additive sheet with the pack normalised to 100,

X = P_W + B_W , Y = P_L + B_L , X-Y = P_W - P_L + B_W - B_L

and P_W + P_L = 100. The trick material can be made essentially one-sided and it can be made one-sided with the winning pair finishing third and fourth to empty, so in the idealised limit

P_W^max = 100 , P_L^min = 0 , P_W - P_L = 100

is attainable under the hypothesis O_W = 0. That 100 already is the card differential for winning the hand; there is no independent hand-win premium left to add on top of it in the P+B normalisation.

Going out is forced by hypothesis. Winner does not go out first or second, so O_W = 0 and the first and second out bonuses are forced onto the loser. On the commercial 100/100 first/second out convention used in the standard literature that is

O_L = 100 + 100 = 200 , O_W - O_L = -200

on X-Y.

Tichu is per player. The point-win compatible extremum is two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side:

B_W^T,max = 2 × 200 = +400
B_L^T,min = 2 × (-200) = -400

so B_W - B_L = 800 on bonuses alone.

Hence on the P+B board

X_max = P_W^max + B_W^T,max = 100 + 400 = 500
Y_min = P_L^min + O_L + B_L^T,min = 0 + 200 - 400 = -200

and in signed board terms

X_max - Y_min = 500 - (-200) = 700
= 100_card + 400_2 succ Grand + 400_2 fail Grand - 200_forced 1st/2nd out.

That is the textbook 500 vs -200 board, attainable with Wc = 100, Lc = 0, two successful Grand Tichus for the winners and two failed Grand Tichus for the losers, winner third/fourth out.

The 800 nominal figures that keep appearing are the same construction with the +100 hand-win premium written explicitly on top of the P_W - P_L = 100 card differential that is already embodied in the normalisation. In the P+B normalisation that is double counting.

The 750/850 numbers that are mentioned are the 100/50 second-out house variant, O_L = 100 + 50 = 150. With that house rule the out debit is -150 and you do get 750 net, 850 nominal with the explicit win premium. That is a legitimate club variation, but it is not the standard 100/100 first/second out convention used in the commercial literature that the question refers to. Staying with the standard 100/100 out, the forced out debit is 200 and the attainable supremum under winner not first/second out is the 700 point signed gap, 500 for the winner against -200 for the loser.

2.text:
With the pack normalised to $P_W+P_L=100$ on the ordinary additive
$P+B+O$ sheet

$$
X=P_W+B_W+O_W ,\qquad Y=P_L+B_L+O_L ,\qquad 
X-Y=P_W-P_L+B_W-B_L+O_W-O_L .
$$

The card material can be made essentially one sided and it can be made
one sided with the winning pair $3\!-\!4$ to empty.  In the idealised
limit, compatible with $O_W=0$,

$$
P_W^{\max}=100,\qquad P_L^{\min}=0,\qquad P_W-P_L=100,
$$

and the $100$ is the whole card contribution to $X-Y$. The hand win is
already embodied in $P_W+P_L=100$.

First/second out.  On the commercial $100/100$ convention the hypothesis
$W$ not $1/2$ out forces

$$
O_W=0,\qquad O_L=100+100=200,\qquad O_W-O_L=-200
$$

on $X-Y$.

One Tichu call per player.  The point-win compatible extremum is

$$
B_W^{T,\max}=2\,{\rm Grand}=2\times200=+400,\qquad
B_L^{T,\min}=2\,{\rm failed\;Grand}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

i.e. $B_W-B_L=800$ on bonuses alone.

Hence on the $P+B+O$ board

$$
X_{\max}=P_W^{\max}+B_W^{T,\max}+O_W=100+400+0=500,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=P_L^{\min}+B_L^{T,\min}+O_L=0-400+200=-200,
$$

so in signed board terms

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
=100_{\rm card}+400_{2\,{\rm succ\,Grand}}+400_{2\,{\rm fail\,Grand}}
-200_{1^{st}/2^{nd}\,out},
$$

$100$ points of pure card swing, $+400$ points for two successful Grand
Tichus on the winners and a further $+400$ points taken out of the losers
by two failed Grand Tichus, offset by the $200$ points of first/second
out forced onto the losing side.  That is the textbook $500$ vs $-200$
board, $300$ points with ordinary Tichu, attainable with $W_c=100$,
$L_c=0$, two successful Grand Tichus for the winners, two failed Grand
Tichus for the losers and the winner third/fourth out.

Remark on book-keeping.  If the $+100$ hand-win premium is written as an
explicit additive term on top of the $P_W-P_L=100$ card differential the
nominal totals are $X^{nom}_{\max}=100_c+100_{win}+400_T=600$ and
$Y^{nom}_{\min}=-200$, i.e. the familiar nominal spread
$600-(-200)=800$.  The extra $100$ is the inessential $P_W+P_L=100$
complement already absorbed in the $P_W-P_L=100$ normalisation; removing
the double count gives the $700$ point signed, $500$ vs $-200$, supremum
quoted for the standard $100/100$ first/second out game.  On the
$100/50$ second-out house variant $O_L=150$ this becomes $750$ net,
$850$ nominal. ∎

is attainable under the hypothesis O_W = 0. That 100 already is the card differential for winning the hand; there is no independent hand-win premium left to add on top of it in the P+B normalisation.

on X-Y.

Y_min = P_L^min + O_L + B_L^T,min = 0 + 200 - 400 = -200
